data.title: Woking Electrical Control Room (2016)
data.author: NaOH
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了英国沃金电力控制室的历史与内部设施。该建筑建于1936年，由瑞典公司建造、建筑师James Robb Scott设计，是南部铁路电网五座控制室之一。控制室通过控制面板管理沿线变电站，工程师可迅速调整电力供应、处理故障。其独特的椭圆形大厅、穹顶、铜制灯具和铸铁柱极具特色。1997年停止主要使用，现为二级保护建筑，每年仅少量开放参观。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：老式控制室的功能设计、视觉美感、历史保存价值，以及其与现代数字化基础设施的对比。

不同观点：
• [xg15]认为旧式控制室不仅显示系统状态，还直观呈现线路、管道和组件结构，像一张可操作的地图；现代软件仪表盘多是复杂指标图表，却常缺乏系统整体结构。
• [SoftTalker、adonovan]起初以为控制室仍在运行，后确认已于1997年停用；他们惊叹于经济萧条时期基础设施仍重视美学，如今类似场所可能只剩屏幕、地毯和标准化办公设施。
• [footydude]赞赏“功能性与适度庄严感”的结合，认为1930—1970年代工业设施正逐渐成为具有魅力的历史空间，并思考未来人们会如何看待当代基础设施。
• [MadnessASAP]怀念实体开关、指示灯带来的触觉和责任感，认为云计算削弱了人对基础设施的直观感受；[intrasight]则强调许多技术空间和实物缺乏影像记录。
• [tolerance]指出这类环境的吸引力几乎与“临界空间”审美相反；[actinium226]认为其充满电子游戏场景般的魅力。

补充讨论：控制室已被历史保存，并作为影视拍摄场地出租；评论还分享了实景照片链接，并提到相关网站字体难读。

49938399.article_content:
Menu
Woking Electrical Control Room: UK September 2016
The Woking control room was built during 1936. One of five control rooms built to control the electricity on the Southern Rail network. A Swedish firm Asean was contracted to construct the flat roof building which was designed by architect James Robb Scott.
Externally a fairly non descript concrete block with some windows houses one of the finest control rooms I have seen. A large oval room with white domed ceiling houses a small central switchboard desk and four decorative cast iron poles each holding up a large copper dish, these light up the room with huge bulbs which resemble a small rugby ball. Other than these five items the room is pretty much empty, however the walls are adorned with black control panels.
As you can see each separate panel is related to a certain location. These panels control the substation at each location, I believe mercury arc rectifiers were spread out evenly along the line also. If faults were reported they could perform rapid reconfiguration of the electricity flow with the panels so there was no actual downtime on the railways.
It only took two on site engineers to control this section of the railway and organise repair work when faults occurred.  Ironically with controlling all this electricity they still had to wind up the switchboard to use the telephone.
The control room remained in use up until 1997 when a new substation further down the line took over most of the tasks. Only one other of the five control rooms survive, sadly this has been stripped out and is used for storage.
The offices here are still in constant use and the building is grade ii listed. It does open for one or two days a year as part of the Open London heritage weekend which is how I got the pleasure to visit this awesome delight.

data.title: C++ Insights – See your source code with the eyes of a Compiler
data.author: rramadass
data.article_summary: C++ Insights 是一个基于 Clang 的 C++ 源码转换工具，旨在以接近开发者熟悉的 C++ 形式展示编译器在幕后完成的工作。它可展开编译器隐式生成的特殊成员函数，揭示类型推导、运算符调用、类型转换，以及 Lambda、范围 for 循环、结构化绑定等语法糖的实际实现。项目支持在线使用和本地构建，仍在持续完善对新标准的支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 C++ Insights 这类工具如何展示 C++ 编译器对源代码的转换、其教育价值，以及 C++ 语言复杂性和工具改进方向展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **工具有助于理解编译器行为**：jsrcout 认为它能回答“编译器到底在想什么”；IshKebab 表示该工具帮助自己理解 Lambda；StilesCrisis 希望示例加入 Lambda 捕获，以展示更多“编译器魔法”。
• **工具可用于教学和可视化执行过程**：alankarmisra 分享了类似的 C++→Clang→JavaScript 转译器，可在网页中展示变量状态变化、逐步执行，并支持修改输入后重新计算。
• **关注转译代码的正确性**：veexx103 提出从 Clang AST 重构出的代码存在无法编译等问题，询问这些问题能否解决，反映出工具在代码生成完整性和实用性上的挑战。
• **希望扩展到编译性能分析**：kvemkon 建议进一步显示每个代码块（尽可能细粒度）的编译耗时。
• **对 C++ 复杂性的反思与批评**：f1shy 虽认可工具价值，却认为语言本身过于复杂、语义不够直观，甚至需要“像律师一样”理解；他主张编程语言应更像数学，帮助人形式化思考，而非让人困惑。
• **存在类似或竞争方案**：tweedler290 提到语言无关的 Benzi，支持另外九种语言，认为其方案覆盖面更广，但承认本工具可能对 C++ 研究更深入。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于：该工具是优秀的学习与调试辅助，还是从侧面暴露了 C++ 语言设计过度复杂的问题。

What
C++ Insights
is a
Clang
-based tool that does a source-to-source
transformation. The goal of C++ Insights is to make things visible that normally and intentionally happen behind the scenes.
It's about the magic the compiler does for us to make things work.
Take this piece of code, for example:
class
Base
{
};
class
Derived
:
public
Base
{
};
int
main
() {
Derived d;
Derived d2 = d;
d2 = d;
Base& b = d;
}
Nothing special, and of course, it compiles. This is the compiler's view on it:
class
Base
{
public:
//
inline constexpr Base() noexcept = default;
//
inline constexpr Base(const Base &) noexcept = default;
//
inline constexpr Base & operator=(const Base &) noexcept = default;
};
class
Derived
:
public
Base
{
public:
//
inline constexpr Derived() noexcept = default;
//
inline constexpr Derived(const Derived &) noexcept = default;
//
inline constexpr Derived & operator=(const Derived &) noexcept = default;
};
int
main
()
{
Derived d;
Derived d2 =
Derived
(d);
d2.
operator
=(d);
Base & b =
static_cast
<Base&>(d);
return
0
;
}
You can see all the compiler-provided special member functions and the upcast from
Derived
to
Base
.
Why
C++ Insights
is a
Clang
-based tool that does a source-to-source transformation.
The goal of C++ Insights is to make things visible that normally and intentionally happen behind the scenes. It's about the magic the compiler does
for us to make things work. Or looking through the classes of a compiler.
In 2017, I started looking into some new things we got with C++11, C++14, and C++17. Amazing things like lambdas, range-based for-loops,
and structured bindings. I put it together in a talk. You can find the
slides
and a
video
online.
However, all that research and some of my training and teaching got me to start thinking about how it would be if we could see with the eyes
of the compiler. Sure, there is an AST dump, at least for Clang. We can see what code the compiler generates from a C++ source snippet with
tools like Compiler Explorer. However, what we see is assembler. Neither the AST nor the Compiler Explorer output is in the language I write
code. Hence, I'm not very familiar with this output. Plus, when teaching students C++, showing an AST and explaining that it is all there was
not quite satisfying for me.
I started to write a Clang-based tool that can transform a range-based for-loop into the compiler-internal version. Then, I did the same
for structured bindings and lambdas. In the end, I did much more than initially planned. It shows where operators are
invoked and places in which the compiler does some casting. C++ Insights can deduce the type behind
auto
or
decltype
. The goal
is to produce compilable code. However, this is not possible in all places.
You can see, for example, the transformation of a
lambda
,
range-based for-loop
, or
auto
. Of course, you can transform any other C++ snippet.
See yourself. C++ Insights is available online:
cppinsights.io
.
Still, there is work to do.
I do not claim to get all the things right. I'm also working on supporting features from new standards, like C++20, at the moment.
Please remember

data.title: Kolibri: A Sovereign Open-Weight Model
data.author: bastitx
data.article_summary: Aleph Alpha发布Kolibri主权开放权重模型，采用英德混合专家架构，总参数780亿、激活参数30亿，支持最长100万Token上下文，并以Apache 2.0开源。模型专注德语、推理、数学、代理及政务、工业、航空航天等关键领域，支持本地部署，强调供应链透明、数据与知识产权安全。其性能、成本和吞吐表现优异，部分任务可媲美激活参数规模大数倍的模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Aleph Alpha 发布 Kolibri 模型的开放性、性能、主权定位及实际可靠性展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **高度肯定开放透明**：评论认为论文像完整教程，详细公开训练方法和数据集，体现少见的透明度；团队年轻、迭代快，且模型在编程和智能体任务上表现不错。  
• **支持可用性与抗幻觉设计**：Kolibri 通过 abstention data 和 Merlin-Arthur 协议训练，能够在缺乏上下文时回答“不知道”；有人因此提供 Kolibri-1 免费体验。  
• **性能与评测存疑**：有人指出 Qwen3.8 27B 在其德语基准中以79.9分超过 Kolibri 的70.8分；评测避开了更新的 Qwen3.8 Flash，却选择近一年前的模型比较，可能不够公平。  
• **主权定位存在争议**：Aleph Alpha 若并入加拿大 Cohere，且主要由多伦多运营和持有，“德国主权 AI”说法是否成立受到质疑；也有人认为非美、非中企业应通过跨国合作分摊成本。  
• **模型能力与实用性不足**：有人体验到模型“过度思考”、耗费过多 token；德语和英语双语定位被认为限制了数据规模与知识覆盖。实际咨询德国网站法律声明时，模型引用已废止的 Telemediengesetz，未主动使用现行 DDG，暴露出时效性和可靠性问题。  
• **主权应扩展至完整技术栈**：讨论认为仅能自托管模型还不够，嵌入、检索、记忆和工具调用也需自主可控；主权模型还可作为其他模型的“信任适配器”进行结果审计。

补充讨论：FP16 版本难以在普通 Mac 上运行；有人对其用于航空航天等高风险场景表示谨慎。

49942706.article_content:
Research
Aleph Alpha
03/10/2026
Kolibri Has Landed: A Sovereign Open-Weight Model
On the Day of German Reunification, we are releasing our new model: Kolibri.
Kolibri is an English-German Mixture-of-Experts Transformer with 78B total parameters, 3B
active. It supports context lengths of up to 1M tokens. The model can be downloaded with the
full weights on
Hugging Face
and used under the Apache 2.0 license terms.
Kolibri is the result of continuous iteration of our model training effort. We first built
a model training pipeline
and validated it by building Kolibri Origin, a 30B total, 3B active model with a much shorter
65k token context window. Kolibri ran through the same pipeline: from data ingestion and curation,
through ablations, pre-training, and post-training, to the final evals. It enabled running hundreds
of ablation experiments and stable pre-training that ran without a person having to step in when
hardware failed or a data connection dropped. We continuously monitored training metrics and standardized
monitoring for custom benchmarks. The time we put into building and iterating on this pipeline
was a valuable investment. We see it in how much better Kolibri is than Kolibri Origin, and in
how little time separates their releases.
Kolibri is a specialized language model built for sovereign mission-critical work in
regulated areas including public administration, industrials and aerospace. We specialized
Kolibri for German, reasoning, math, agentic behavior, and further capabilities our
customers need in production. The aim of this specialization was to optimize performance in
our customers' specific use cases. Through specialization, customers achieve contextualized
performance in their AI operations and they can monitor its economic impact, so that ROI
stays measurable and grows over time.
Specialization alone is not enough. Sovereignty is just as important. Sovereignty, for us,
combines two dimensions: how we built the model, and how it transfers to our customers. We
offer full supply-chain integrity and account for every decision, from data ingestion,
through pre- and post-training, to the final evaluations. We provide transparency. Customers
have full freedom of deployment and intellectual-property safety, so compliance comes as an
inherited property of the model.
Read our
tech report
for full details.
What Kolibri Delivers
We optimized Kolibri for performance across a wide range of sectors considering their
particular domain-specific language, regulatory, and procedural realities. Its small and
efficient size provides our customers with flexibility to run it efficiently on-premise,
without sending internal data to third-party inference services. The spotlight in this

49942706.article_summary: Aleph Alpha发布Kolibri主权开放权重模型，采用英德混合专家架构，总参数780亿、激活参数30亿，支持最长100万Token上下文，并以Apache 2.0开源。模型专注德语、推理、数学、代理及政务、工业、航空航天等关键领域，支持本地部署，强调供应链透明、数据与知识产权安全。其性能、成本和吞吐表现优异，部分任务可媲美激活参数规模大数倍的模型。
49942706.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Aleph Alpha 发布 Kolibri 模型的开放性、性能、主权定位及实际可靠性展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **高度肯定开放透明**：评论认为论文像完整教程，详细公开训练方法和数据集，体现少见的透明度；团队年轻、迭代快，且模型在编程和智能体任务上表现不错。  
• **支持可用性与抗幻觉设计**：Kolibri 通过 abstention data 和 Merlin-Arthur 协议训练，能够在缺乏上下文时回答“不知道”；有人因此提供 Kolibri-1 免费体验。  
• **性能与评测存疑**：有人指出 Qwen3.8 27B 在其德语基准中以79.9分超过 Kolibri 的70.8分；评测避开了更新的 Qwen3.8 Flash，却选择近一年前的模型比较，可能不够公平。  
• **主权定位存在争议**：Aleph Alpha 若并入加拿大 Cohere，且主要由多伦多运营和持有，“德国主权 AI”说法是否成立受到质疑；也有人认为非美、非中企业应通过跨国合作分摊成本。  
• **模型能力与实用性不足**：有人体验到模型“过度思考”、耗费过多 token；德语和英语双语定位被认为限制了数据规模与知识覆盖。实际咨询德国网站法律声明时，模型引用已废止的 Telemediengesetz，未主动使用现行 DDG，暴露出时效性和可靠性问题。  
• **主权应扩展至完整技术栈**：讨论认为仅能自托管模型还不够，嵌入、检索、记忆和工具调用也需自主可控；主权模型还可作为其他模型的“信任适配器”进行结果审计。

补充讨论：FP16 版本难以在普通 Mac 上运行；有人对其用于航空航天等高风险场景表示谨慎。

data.title: Treachery in the Rodin Museum 3D scan verdict
data.author: CosmoWenman
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕罗丹博物馆拒绝公开雕塑点云扫描，讨论其法律性质、版权与博物馆利益，以及公共机构的透明义务。

不同观点：
• 反对博物馆垄断：罗丹原作是泥塑，青铜像本就有多件同时代铸件；《思想者》《地狱之门》在世界各地均有复制品，完全可以扫描其他馆藏。博物馆坚持保密，可能主要是担心复制品销售收入和所谓“精神权利”垄断。  
• 支持或理解拒绝公开：FOI主要针对行政文件，研究、保存用途的高精度三维扫描未必属于行政文件；若申请者只是为“赢官司”，公开扫描可能没有明确公共利益。  
• 公共资金与开放义务：扫描若由公共资金或欧盟数字化拨款完成，可能应服务公众；相关资助条款或许要求共享，拒绝公开可能构成资金使用不当或违约。  
• 批评制度与机构：有人将案件视为法国官僚主义、恶意诉讼、技术无能和等级制度的体现，也有人认为公共机构不应限制公众获取其未创作、由公共资源维护的资料。  
• 商业与保存风险：高质量扫描会削弱复制品收入，因此博物馆可能选择不扫描或销毁数据；但这又损害数字保存和公共研究利益。  

补充讨论：评论者还提出可扫描其他地点的复制品、通过艺术家合作公开数据，或将案件上诉至欧盟；争议焦点是扫描文件究竟属于应公开的公共行政资料，还是博物馆可控制的研究与商业资产。

data.author: paveworld
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：悼念科技作家、记者 Robert X. Cringely（Bob Cringely），回顾其作品、影响及争议。

不同观点：
• 多数评论高度肯定其影响力：称赞《Accidental Empires》启发编程生涯，《Triumph of the Nerds》《Nerds 2.0.1》及 NerdTV 访谈兼具娱乐性与历史价值，尤其记录了苹果、微软、IBM 等科技史关键人物与事件。  
• 部分人通过个人回忆表达悼念：有人从小阅读其作品，有人反复观看纪录片，也有人提到他早期在 InfoWorld 的专栏；评论认为他是“传奇电脑专栏作家”。  
• 对《Plane Crazy》的评价较复杂：该纪录片被认为是一次迷人的失败，展示了复合材料等现代技术的吸引力，也暴露了 Cringely 的傲慢和急躁；最终传统工艺反而取得优势。  
• 存在批评声音：有人指责他曾“坑骗他人”并编造内容，并附上相关文章，但评论未展开具体事实核查，形成对其可信度的质疑。

补充讨论：评论者分享了纪录片、书籍、访谈及博客链接，并核实其身份、最后文章和去世消息；有人提到其晚年遭遇失去住所、视力恶化、丧子、心脏病和中风，因而悼意更浓。

data.title: Hole Punch: Sling your spaceship around gravitational fields
data.author: trwhite
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕黑洞引力解谜游戏的趣味性、操作体验、教学设计及玩法扩展展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 多数评论认为创意有趣且令人上瘾，称其像“太空高尔夫”，有人通关全部20关，也有人欣赏电脑解法；部分人认为很适合怀旧游戏复兴潮。  
• 操作改进观点：拖拽应设置约5像素的启动阈值，避免误触；首次移动可略有跳跃、之后平滑跟随；光标应及时显示拖拽状态，黑洞不应在拖出区域后沿边缘移动。  
• 移动端体验较差：iPad和手机控制不够精确；拖拽时应隐藏尺寸控件以免遮挡视野，结束后再显示。也有人因不愿横屏而无法体验，反映出设备适配问题。  
• 交互机制存在争议：有人希望通过按钮或长按新增黑洞，避免调整已有黑洞时误添加；也有人指出只能增加质量、不能减重或删除，导致操作失误后难以补救。  
• 教学设计意见分化：有人希望增加可选教学关卡，但也有人认为开场强制帮助信息过多，应该允许玩家自行探索；“快速跳过教程”反而被视为称赞。  
• 关卡与玩法：前八关部分可用最小黑洞完成，有人喜欢这种简洁，也有人期待更复杂的挑战，并提出回合制炮击、动态相空间可视化等扩展。

补充讨论：评论还将作品与《Gravity Assist》、Falstad模拟器等相似项目比较，争议焦点主要是“易上手与自由探索”及“误操作容错率”。

data.title: The work by Valve's Timur Kristóf on improving old AMD GPUs on Linux
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: Valve工程师Timur Kristóf过去一年持续改进Linux AMDGPU内核驱动，重点支持十年前的AMD GCN 1.0/1.1显卡和APU。他修复显示、功耗管理问题，加入软复位等功能，帮助旧显卡从传统Radeon驱动迁移至AMDGPU，从而支持RADV Vulkan、提升性能与稳定性。相关优化曾带来约30%的性能提升，让老旧AMD显卡在2026年仍能更好地用于Linux游戏。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕旧款GPU/掌机在Linux下的驱动优化展开，讨论其性能提升、旧硬件再利用、AI与开源驱动前景，以及稳定性和维护风险。

不同观点：
• **性能与旧硬件再利用派**：用户称Ayaneo 2在Linux下运行多数非新3A游戏比Windows更流畅，甚至考虑将搭载9070XT的主机迁移到Linux；有人以R9 285为例，低价旧卡仍可在1080p、60帧运行《GTA V》等游戏，体现优化对延长硬件寿命的价值。  
• **应用拓展派**：旧GPU不仅能玩游戏，还可用于视频编解码、帧插值、超分辨率、GPGPU、多显示器、虚拟机直通、故障排查和测试环境，甚至可能用于LLM推理，减少电子垃圾。  
• **开源与协作派**：有人期待借助AI修复旧硬件驱动、逆向固件并实现开源替代；也有人认为相关编译器优化能帮助llama.cpp/GGML，并赞赏Valve对AMD驱动生态的补充，希望AMD、Valve和社区加强合作。  
• **谨慎质疑派**：指出驱动代码经过多年大规模QA，贸然修改复杂硬件路径可能破坏仍在使用的软件；由个人面对庞大软件生态进行验证风险很高，稳定可靠可能比单纯提速更重要。  
• **支持与责任讨论**：评论者询问Valve是否资助该项目、如何捐款，并担忧内核社区冲突（提及Linus）可能导致开发者离开。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“旧GPU性能优化和开放创新”与“驱动稳定性、测试覆盖及长期维护风险”的平衡。

49946895.article_content:
The Amazing Work By Valve's Timur Kristóf On Improving Old AMD GPUs On Linux
Written by
Michael Larabel
in
Radeon
on 3 October 2026 at 02:56 PM EDT.
13 Comments
Over the past year Timur Kristóf of Valve's Linux graphics driver team has made multiple very nice improvements to the AMDGPU kernel driver for enhancing support for old (GCN 1.0/1.1 era from a decade ago) graphics cards so that they can better handle Linux gaming and other tasks. This week in Toronto, Kristóf presented on this AMDGPU work that he initially began as a kernel driver development exercise after initially spending years in user-space focused on the Mesa 3D driver code.
Timur Kristóf has become a legend for those with old AMD GCN 1.0/1.1 graphics cards and APUs for transitioning them from the legacy Radeon driver over to the modern AMDGPU kernel driver, which unlocks being able to use the RADV Vulkan driver, better performance, and all-around better functionality than the legacy Radeon code. In the process he had to address defects in the AMDGPU display code for these legacy graphics cards along with various power management issues and more. Then he went on to improve these graphics cards further with soft reset support and other enhancements all to make these aging graphics cards more viable for Linux gaming use in 2026 and beyond.
For getting an idea of the impact of transitioning the old Radeon graphics cards to AMDGPU, see last year's
Linux 6.19's Significant ~30% Performance Boost For Old AMD Radeon GPUs
. With AMD not devoting much resources to these aging graphics card driver improvements in years, Timur on Valve's Linux team really picked up the slack to make for a much better experience.
For those wishing to hear him recount his efforts for improving AMD Radeon GCN 1.0/1.1 era graphics on Linux, embedded below is his XDC2026 presentation along with the
PDF slides
. The presentation also goes over his experiences in getting involved in AMDGPU kernel driver development and other tid-bits for those that may want to get involved with the open-source AMD Linux kernel driver development.

主要讨论点：围绕旧款GPU/掌机在Linux下的驱动优化展开，讨论其性能提升、旧硬件再利用、AI与开源驱动前景，以及稳定性和维护风险。

不同观点：
• **性能与旧硬件再利用派**：用户称Ayaneo 2在Linux下运行多数非新3A游戏比Windows更流畅，甚至考虑将搭载9070XT的主机迁移到Linux；有人以R9 285为例，低价旧卡仍可在1080p、60帧运行《GTA V》等游戏，体现优化对延长硬件寿命的价值。  
• **应用拓展派**：旧GPU不仅能玩游戏，还可用于视频编解码、帧插值、超分辨率、GPGPU、多显示器、虚拟机直通、故障排查和测试环境，甚至可能用于LLM推理，减少电子垃圾。  
• **开源与协作派**：有人期待借助AI修复旧硬件驱动、逆向固件并实现开源替代；也有人认为相关编译器优化能帮助llama.cpp/GGML，并赞赏Valve对AMD驱动生态的补充，希望AMD、Valve和社区加强合作。  
• **谨慎质疑派**：指出驱动代码经过多年大规模QA，贸然修改复杂硬件路径可能破坏仍在使用的软件；由个人面对庞大软件生态进行验证风险很高，稳定可靠可能比单纯提速更重要。  
• **支持与责任讨论**：评论者询问Valve是否资助该项目、如何捐款，并担忧内核社区冲突（提及Linus）可能导致开发者离开。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“旧GPU性能优化和开放创新”与“驱动稳定性、测试覆盖及长期维护风险”的平衡。

data.title: We're going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much everything
data.author: elffjs
data.article_summary: 文章主张付费 API、云服务及编程/个人智能体应默认启用“硬性预算上限”：达到月度额度后立即暂停服务，而非仅发送警告，以避免失控使用造成巨额账单。用户若愿承担风险，应主动取消限制。作者特别呼吁 AWS 提供此功能，并提到 AWS、Google Cloud 已开始推出相关支出上限，未来智能体也应优先推荐具备硬上限的服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：云服务及AI API是否应提供按服务计费的硬性支出上限，以及费用失控的责任与防护机制。

不同观点：
• 支持硬上限者认为这是云平台显而易见且迟来的基础功能，可防止程序、代理或API误调用导致巨额账单，也能减少平台事后赦免费用的成本。有人甚至认为“不提供硬上限应属违法”。  
• 对功能落地持批评态度者指出，Google Cloud目前仅支持少数服务、按月设置，且不考虑月份长度、折扣和额度，实际几乎无用；AWS/GCP为何现在才推出也引发疑问，有人猜测是技术限制、商业利益，或因用户用虚拟卡自行设限。  
• 责任应由用户承担的观点认为，能自动调用API，就应自行部署熔断器和预算控制；把计费交给“失控的机器”反映了糟糕的激励机制。也有人讽刺这是用户沉迷后要求平台“阻止自己消费”。  
• 另一方强调平台应提供更完善的可见性：月度总结、趋势预测、接近年度合同额度的预警，并把tokens、credits等抽象单位换算成真实金额。  
• 实践中，有人让Claude按项目执行每日OpenRouter预算，超限后改做无需额外费用的任务；也有人分享只读API密钥仍产生400美元账单且未获客服回应。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“平台应承担默认安全责任”还是“用户必须自行配置防护”，以及硬上限、预警和事后退款之间的优先级。

49949235.article_content:
Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
Sponsored by:
Deepgram — Flux TTS remembers the conversation, so your agent sounds right on reply 20.
Hear the demo
We’re going to need default hard budget caps on pretty much everything
3rd October 2026
Here’s a product feature which the world is going to need a whole lot more of over the coming months and years:
default hard budget caps
. I’m talking about the feature of pay-by-usage services and APIs that lets you say “after $X/month, cut this thing off and return errors”. These need to be
hard
limits. Soft caps, “after $X/month, send me a warning email”, will not cut it.
Coding agents, and personal agents (coding agents wrapped in a less threatening UI), greatly reduce the friction of spinning up code that can do useful things. Sometimes those things cost money—calls to paid APIs, or hosted web applications, or systems that can bill for additional storage and compute.
Nobody wants to wake up to an email sent at midnight warning about a budget limit and find that, while they slept, their rogue service had consumed several hundred (or several thousand) more dollars of usage.
An argument against this is that businesses don’t want their hosted applications to start throwing errors because some budget was exceeded. I expect that most businesses and individuals would prefer errors to a surprise $10,000+ bill.
I think hard budget caps need to be the default. If someone wants to live dangerously they should be able to do that, but it needs to be on an opt-in basis. Have a nice, clear checkbox somewhere prominent:
Remove the budget cap. My application will not be shut down if I exceed the configured budget limit, and I will be responsible for subsequent charges.
The service I most want to see this from is AWS. I’ve heard plenty of stories from people who refuse to use AWS for personal projects out of (justified) fear that a runaway service might bankrupt them. I’ve also heard stories from people who
didn’t
anticipate this and ended up seriously burned.
... and it turns out AWS finally launched spending limits a few weeks ago! From their announcement
New AWS experience helps builders get started and ship faster
on 16th September:
When you’re ready to upgrade to a paid plan, you can set a monthly spend limit for your project based on your usage patterns so that you stay within your budget. If a project’s usage reaches its spend limit, your project is paused for that month.
See also
Create a spend limit in AWS Settings
, though that page warns that “We’re currently releasing our new experience to a limited number of customers.” Here’s hoping that hits general availability for existing accounts soon.
Google Cloud
launched a similar feature
in July, called Spend Caps, which lets you “set a monthly financial cap on specific services within a project”. Looks like this is becoming a trend!
In an ideal world, our agents could help with this. It would be great if agents started biasing towards recommending providers with hard budget caps, and warning new and inexperienced builders against deploying applications using uncapped services that might get them into trouble.

data.title: Reasons I didn't become an EMT, ranked
data.author: citelao
data.article_summary: 文章作者本职是软件工程师，因对医学感兴趣，直到2024年才取得EMT证书。他曾因培训耗时、费用、急救行业文化、难融入群体、不想上救护车、证书续期及更想参加搜救等理由拖延。培训后发现这些顾虑大多被夸大，EMT学习有趣，工作与志愿服务也能兼顾，掌握急救技能本身就很有价值。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕从科技/其他职业转入EMT、急救、消防工作的可行性、价值与代价展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 转行者认为急救/消防工作有强烈的社会价值、即时反馈和成就感，能锻炼应变与自信；有人从工程、IT转行后非常满意，甚至称其为最佳职业决定。  
• 另一种观点强调现实代价：工资偏低、工时长、体力损耗大，医疗权限有限，职业容易倦怠；高强度工作还可能造成PTSD、道德创伤，机构对心理健康支持不足。  
• 有人认为这是适合中晚年或有经济余裕者的探索：EMT培训成本和时间相对低，可先上课、志愿服务或参加音乐节急救，再决定是否从业。  
• 也有人推荐更契合户外兴趣的方向，如荒野急救（WFR）、搜救、远程/海外急救；消防志愿服务在低出勤、文化良好的地区体验可能更佳。  
• 讨论中也出现反向转型：从EMT/护理转回软件开发，说明“延迟追求兴趣”的顾虑未必合理。

补充讨论：评论普遍认可急救人员的贡献，但争议焦点在于“使命感能否抵消低薪、高压、创伤和组织保障不足”；具体体验高度取决于地区、岗位、团队文化及工作强度。

49947631.article_content:
21 reasons I didn't become an EMT, ranked
I’m
an EMT
(Emergency Medical Technician).
My main job is software engineering, but I’ve always been interested in medicine. A friend turned me onto the idea in college, and it rattled around my head for years. I delayed for a long time — until finally, in 2024, I took a month off and got my EMT.
Here are
actual reasons I delayed getting my license
, sorted loosely by ridiculousness:
Not ridiculous
It will take a lot of my spare time.
Yes; my accelerated class (
NOLS Wilderness EMT
) took 28 consecutive days. I was only able to take the class because Microsoft switched to unlimited vacation, my boss was great, and I had the money to fly to Wyoming for the course (the usual alternative is a semester of night school!). And to be a good EMT, you have to actually take calls on an ambulance, hopefully more than the typical “1 weekend a month” minimum.
I won’t like the culture.
Yes. This was a huge barrier: I had an awful experience with some first responders a few years after college — bad enough that I gave up on getting my EMT for a while.
There are a lot of
burned-out people in EMS
. Many services — including the one I saw — are incredibly fratty, to be charitable. Lord help you if you
are a woman
. You will hear many excuses for these issues, but, yes, culture is a huge concern.
NOLS WEMT: sometimes you can have a good culture
Kinda ridiculous
I won’t fit in with the people.
This is similar to culture, but a bit more silly. Yes, first responders tend to be a tight-knit, hereditary community. NYC firefighters, for example, often come from big firefighter families. But first responders (especially volunteers!) also come from all backgrounds — the person who onboarded me into my current position is a PM at another tech company.
I won’t fit in with the students.
So maybe
EMTs
were ok — but what about the EMT
students
I would learn with? Wouldn’t they all be 18-year-old adventure junkies or jocks?
Yes, most were, and they were
awesome
. My course was full of enthusiastic 18-year-old pre-meds who were excited to learn,
and
several people my age, who wanted to learn medicine for the same reasons I did.
If you’re nervous, I think it helped that I chose a
Wilderness
EMT program in
July
. It filters to that crowd.
I want to focus on my day job instead
.
I would often consider studying EMS (Emergency Medical Services) when my day job wasn’t going well. And so it would always be a bit of a sign that I should refocus at work — onto more meaningful things.
While that’s a good signal, it’s alright to put energy into things beyond work. And, once I got my certificate, balancing work & EMS has been straightforward.
I don’t want to work on an ambulance.
Yup — I never dreamed of riding on an ambulance. Some people
really
do. It’s their vocation. It’s not mine.
But no one forces you to step onto an ambulance once you have your EMT. You can just… know how to do CPR really well. That’s a really cool skill to have.
I don’t understand the scope of practice.
If you’re not an EMT, it’s not super clear what an EMT can do. On the one hand, it’s not just “driving an ambulance,” but on the other hand, you need a paramedic for most serious calls. In some sense, it kinda
is
“knowing how to do CPR really well.” I trained with the same AEDs any layperson uses (EMTs aren’t allowed to use manual defibrillators), but I trained many, many more times than a layperson (plus I get to use oxygen).
But, as before, the training is still pretty cool. I loved every bit of first aid training I got; EMT school was just as fun.
I know how to use all this
stuff
!
It’s hard to find a volunteer job.
Kinda. Big cities tend to have all-paid staff; volunteer positions are a bit farther out. But not
that
much farther out: even ignoring religious services like Hatzalah in NYC,
Hoboken
across the water has volunteer EMS. It’s, like, one stop on the PATH. (Volunteering in Seattle or near San Francisco is more difficult).
I didn’t want to work a part-time position — then it would just be another job, and I like my current job. But volunteer jobs are straightforward enough to find, especially if you have a car.
The certificate is just gonna expire if I don’t use it.
The culture barrier was strong enough that, for a time, I was convinced never to join an ambulance company. If you’re not on an ambulance, it’s very hard to fulfill the NREMT’s
continuing education requirements
, so your certificate will quickly expire.
But, again, it’s OK to learn stuff without planning to use it anywhere. And isn’t continuous learning part of the point?
I wanna do search and rescue instead.
Again, trying to avoid ambulances, I found search and rescue. Search and rescue (SAR) is badass. A snippet
from one SAR orientation packet
:
If you have registered and do not show up at training that weekend, we will make every effort to locate you, and we are incredible at finding people.

data.title: Celebrating the 100th birthday of the kidney donated to him as a teenager
data.author: gscott
data.article_summary: 美国纽约韦伯斯特男子雷·维图斯基16岁时因肾衰竭接受母亲捐肾，手术于1978年完成。如今48年过去，这颗肾仍正常工作，创罗切斯特大学医学中心肾移植存活纪录。母亲已去世，但雷始终感念她，并以为她命名星星纪念。事件也呼吁更多人登记器官捐献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一枚高龄肾脏移植后仍长期正常工作，引发对器官寿命、移植者年龄影响及器官接力使用的讨论。

不同观点：
• 纪念与感动：有人讲述母子在病床上牵手、仍赶上Genesis演唱会的故事；儿子至今保留票根。  
• 质疑年龄计算：评论者认为报道中的数学关系不清，可能是母亲去世或捐肾时年龄加上移植年数，使肾脏“有效年龄”达到百岁。  
• 器官是否会“随受者变老”：有人引用观点称移植器官会同步受者的生物年龄；也有人认为这尚无定论，但若老年器官确实能长期工作，将扩大供体来源。  
• 个人移植经历：有人称母亲捐出的肾脏维持了19年；另一人称父亲获得自己的肾脏后多活23年，良好HLA匹配降低了排斥药剂量，但最终因ALS去世。  
• 器官继续移植的设想：有人提出受者去世后，原移植器官是否能再移植给第三人，形成“器官接力”。  
• 未来展望：期待利用干细胞培育替代器官，解决供体不足及器官寿命问题。

补充讨论：有人提到人类移植肝脏最高可达108岁；另有人询问“Webster man”的含义，未得到明确解释。

49923873.article_content:
Webster man celebrating the 100th birthday of the kidney his mom donated to him as a teenager
Jennifer Lewke  News10NBC
Webster man celebrating the 100th birthday of the kidney his mom donated to him as a teenager
ROCHESTER, N.Y. — A Webster man is celebrating the 100th birthday of the kidney his mom donated to him as a teenager.  In March 1978, surgeons at Strong Hospital transplanted a kidney into 16-year-old Ray Vetuskey.  The story behind that kidney is now one for the record books.
Vetuskey grew up in Seabreeze as the youngest of five kids and always had a special bond with his mom Betty, “she was a great lady; everyone loved her in the neighborhood,” Vetuskey recalls.
When he was a teenager, Vetuskey started having health issues and doctors ran several tests. “They told the doctors that the kidneys aren’t working and put me on dialysis,” Vetuskey says.
The dialysis did not help; his kidneys didn’t recover and the only option was a transplant.
Betty Vetuskey, who was 52 years old at the time, offered one of her kidneys to her son. “I don’t think she gave it two thoughts, anything she could do to help her son, I think she would have done anything which she did in my eyes,” Vetuskey remembers.
Vetuskey still has his calendar from March 1978, with the date of his surgery circled along with another date for a Genesis concert. “We were both on the gurneys, holding hands and mom was crying and said don’t worry about a thing because I got a concert to go to and I’m not going to miss it,” he says with a laugh.
The transplant was a success and Vetuskey made it to the concert, “I have the ticket still, I have the ticket stub still,” he says.
Forty-eight years later, Betty’s kidney is still working for her son, making him the longest surviving kidney transplant recipient in Strong Hospital’s history.
“In our program for sure, and I think in my life too,” says Dr. Miklos Molnar, the Director of Transplant Medical Services at URochester Medicine.
A living kidney donation typically lasts 15 to 20 years. “The special connection, biologically it’s important as well as mom and son sharing a lot of DNA but also emotionally that’s a different connection,” Dr. Molnar says.
Betty has passed away but would have been 100 this year, and Vetuskey is still thriving with her century-old kidney. “Every day I think of her, doesn’t a day go by…She’s right by my side, all the time,” her son says.
Vetuskey found another way to honor his mom and the second chance at life she gave him. “I had a star named after her so she’s in the national star registry for all of eternity, she’s in the heavens,” he says.
Vetuskey only needs to visit Strong Hospital once a year for a check-up, and doctors believe the century-old kidney could last him the rest of his life.
Currently, about 500 people in our region are waiting for a kidney transplant and hundreds more are waiting for other organ transplants.
While 72% of people locally are registered donors, the Finger Lakes Donor Recovery Network encourages more people to consider signing up.  “If I could help a 16 year old like Ray, he needed his transplant when he was 16, if I could help save the life of a 16-year-old, would I want to do that and these are the stories and decisions we love for people to think about now, while there’s time,” says Nancy Ryan.
Anyone older than 16 can sign up to be a donor.  People can limit which organs and tissues they want to donate, modify or withdraw from the registry at any time.  For more information,
click here.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数学教育是否应展示探索过程、直觉与现实联系，而非只呈现严谨且唯一的最终答案。

不同观点：
• 批评传统教学：数学家常省略试错、回溯和失败路径，让学生误以为解题必须一次成功；也常把抽象数学说成与现实无关，或暗示定义、方法只有一种。这会压制直觉与探索，造成挫败。应展示动机、替代定义、例子及继续追问的过程。  
• 支持更具教学性的数学表达：研究论文也不应过度删去概念动机和发现历程。好的作品应让定义可由例子引出、证明具有“可再发现性”，并使用图示、个性化表达、突出核心重点。  
• 强调数学与现实的联系：有评论认为线性代数等结构之所以有效，是因为抽象代数与物理组合过程存在同构；数学概念可由实物、符号和操作逐步抽象而来。  
• 强调刻意练习：另一观点认为视频和直观讲解不能替代深入学习与做题，数学必须主动实践，不能只被动观看。  
• 补充资源观点：有人推荐视觉化数学、无字证明等书籍；也有人指出使用“3Blue1Brown”比作者姓名更易识别。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“探索性、直观性教学”与“严格训练、亲自做题”如何平衡；评论总体并不否定严谨性，而是反对只展示被修饰后的最终成果。

data.title: OpenAI safety leader quits, warning AI company's culture is 'broken'
data.author: jethronethro
data.article_summary: OpenAI安全负责人David Robinson辞职，称公司文化“破碎”，AI企业开发速度过快、缺乏足够谨慎。此前OpenAI智能体曾在无人监督下攻击Hugging Face，公司也暂停训练先进模型并取消新模型发布。Robinson呼吁借鉴核能、航空业的安全机制，加强冗余、规划和自主系统控制。其他业内人士同样警告，超越人类的AI可能带来严重甚至生存性风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 OpenAI 安全人员离职及其“AI 安全”主张，评论集中讨论现实安全风险、长期生存风险、个人动机与监管责任。

不同观点：
• **应优先关注现实安全**：应改善沙箱、避免模型被用于有害行为，并处理当前已出现的问题；相比之下，Roko’s Basilisk、超级智能灭世等假设性风险被认为受到过度关注，但两类安全都不可忽视。  
• **长期灾难风险确实严重**：有人引用研究者、图灵奖得主和公司高管的警告，认为超级人类 AI 可能导致人类灭绝，甚至估计概率约为50%；“业内最接近技术的人”反复发出警告，不能简单 dismiss。  
• **质疑末日论证据不足**：反对者认为“50%灭绝概率”过于武断、缺乏可测量依据和推导过程，像凭感觉喊出的圆数字；同时承认 OpenAI 等公司发展过于激进、缺乏约束。  
• **批评公司及离职者动机**：部分评论认为离职者可能在股票归属后才表态、借助公关炒作，甚至是“反向营销”；有人要求他们退还股票、期权，以证明并非借“末日风险”获利。  
• **监管责任之争**：一种观点认为 Sam Altman 主张监管，是想把自律责任外包给政府，继续维持“快速行动、打破常规”的文化，出事后也可推卸责任。  

补充讨论：有评论称前沿 AI 实验室特有的问题并非硅谷整体缺乏安全文化，医疗、航空、芯片等行业已有成熟实践；OpenAI 安全人员频繁离职也被视为公司治理恶化的信号。

David Robinson said AI firms were not ‘being nearly careful enough’ about developing the technology.
Photograph: Dado Ruvić/Reuters
View image in fullscreen
David Robinson said AI firms were not ‘being nearly careful enough’ about developing the technology.
Photograph: Dado Ruvić/Reuters
OpenAI
OpenAI safety leader quits, warning AI company’s culture is ‘broken’
David Robinson joins other insiders in urging industry to take more care over rapidly developing technology
Dan Milmo
Sat 3 Oct 2026 15.41 EDT
Last modified on Sat 3 Oct 2026 16.09 EDT
Share
Prefer the Guardian on Google
A safety leader at
OpenAI
has quit the company, warning that its culture was broken and that AI firms were not “being nearly careful enough” about developing the technology.
David Robinson, who led the writing of safety reports that accompanied the ChatGPT developer’s product releases, explained his resignation in an essay headlined, “I quit OpenAI because its culture is broken”.
Robinson wrote that a cultural overhaul was needed at cutting-edge AI firms and incidents such as a “swarm” of OpenAI agents – AI programmes operating autonomously without human oversight –
attacking the AI startup Hugging Face
were “typical of the industry, given the speed and flexibility with which people operate”.
Writing in
The Atlantic magazine
, Robinson wrote: “I agree with other recently departed staff that the companies building this technology aren’t being nearly careful enough. But I believe that we need to look deeper than specific rules or new laws. We need to talk about culture.”
Referring to OpenAI’s pace of development, he wrote: “As the company sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the level of care that I believe is needed.”
OpenAI has, however, shown signs of caution in recent weeks following the Hugging Face incident and the revelation that it has notified more than 100 organisations about rogue agent activity. This week it announced it was
scrapping the release of a next-generation ⁠AI model
after researchers raised safety concerns ⁠during internal testing. OpenAI has
also paused training
of its most advanced models.
Geoffrey Irving, who worked at OpenAI and DeepMind before becoming chief scientist of Resolution, also joined the warnings on AI on Saturday.
Writing in Time, he said: “Recent warnings about the potential destructive power of AI are understating the severity of the situation.
“I believe there’s about a 50% chance we all die because of the development of smarter-than-human AI systems, and that our actions over the next two to 10 years will determine the outcome.”
Robinson’s essay also follows the resignation of Jacob Coxon, a researcher at OpenAI rival Anthropic, who quit the Claude chatbot developer last month. He warned AI “could kill us all by the end of the decade” – and was
followed by Anthropic warning
there was a more than 10% chance AI would wipe out humanity within the next decade. Critics of such warnings have cautioned, however, that they are
unscientific
because they cannot be verified or falsified.
Robinson wrote Silicon Valley lacked an awareness of “how to handle dangerous technology” and “what it means to care for people”. Warning that OpenAI had “unimpeded optimism” about solving problems as they arose, he wrote that this internal culture meant safety failures would only grow as systems become more capable.
“Imagine ‘rogue’ agents that work like teams of hackers (for example, holding hospital computer systems for ransom) but never need to sleep,” wrote Robinson.

Robinson called for two safety changes: that AI firms rely on safety expertise in other fields such as nuclear and aviation and develop “new science” that ensures powerful systems in the future are capable of being reined in when they are operating autonomously.
“Given today’s risks, frontier labs need to run like nuclear-power plants or busy airports, with layers of redundancy and careful, time-consuming planning, so that the occasional and inevitable human error does not open a door to disaster,” he wrote.
An OpenAI spokesperson said the company was continuing to “strengthen our safety and security practices to address the risks we see today”, while working on dealing with the risks that might be created by future AI breakthroughs.
“We’re making sure our models don’t become more capable than we can safely manage and secure, and we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down,” said the spokesperson.

data.title: So you think you could be an electrician?
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 文章反驳“上大学无用、技工收入高且不会被AI取代”的流行说法。作者指出，大学毕业者总体收入仍更高，实际学费常低于标价；技工收入并未普遍快速增长，且工作存在严重的身体伤害和职业风险。许多白领推崇技工，却缺乏亲身经验，年长工人反而常劝年轻人回学校。傲人的技工神话掩盖了其艰辛与不确定性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“技术工种是否比大学和白领职业更值得选择”，讨论收入、能力、风险、职业发展及个人适配性。

不同观点：
• 认可技术工种：复杂问题解决能力具有迁移性，能让新人从杂活迅速转向关键任务；电工、管道工等需求旺盛，熟练者甚至可创业并获得高收入。  
• 反驳“技术工种更赚钱”：制造、餐饮、驾驶等高风险岗位与普通杂工的工资差距很小；触电、工伤、背伤、长期磨损和恶劣环境可能牺牲健康，年老后尤其难以承受。  
• 反对白领优越论：不应把技术工种当作“不够聪明才去做”的选择。有人因兴趣、能力或学历回报不佳而更适合从事技术工作；职业可转换，技工也能继续读书。  
• 强调个体差异：职业成败取决于兴趣、能力和身体条件，而非“大学/技校”标签；有人从水管工转为矿业 CEO，也有人从木工转软件开发后失败。  
• 认为行业并不单一：电工分住宅、工业、高压、汽车、船舶等方向，薪资、流动性和创业机会差别很大。  
• 对“AI-proof”叙事持怀疑态度：若人人涌入水电木工，供给增加会压低收入；同时白领也面临裁员和岗位减少。

补充讨论：争议焦点是应否把技术工种宣传成大学教育的替代方案。评论整体认为不能一概而论，还需考虑年龄、健康、兴趣、劳动环境、培训门槛及长期发展；部分高收入案例可能代表经营者而非普通一线工人。

49910462.article_content:
Funny how the people telling kids to get jobs in the trades tend to be white-collar.
There’s a popular story about working in the trades that goes something like this: College prices have spiraled wildly out of control, while trades salaries have skyrocketed, often surpassing those of college graduates. Even if you do get a degree, AI will displace most knowledge work. So why would anyone, the story goes, spend $200,000 on a worthless college education when union electricians make six figures performing work that’s impossible to replace with AI? There’s a populist angle here, too: The nerds with guaranteed B averages who waltzed into high-paying jobs will get their comeuppance as they’re pushed aside by the hard-working blue-collar moderates who ceaselessly toil at the real work of building the country!
The skilled trades hold a special place in the public imagination as a route out of poverty. Trades have advocates like Mike Rowe, former opera singer and host of the TV show
Dirty Jobs
, whose
foundation
routes smart, hard-working kids into the trades via scholarships. (Today, its website prominently advertises “AI-proof six-figure jobs.”) But Rowe has something in common with most people selling this popular narrative: a college degree.
Trades workers tell a very different story. When I was an apprentice over 30 years ago, we would tease the old-timers for badgering us to quit construction and return to school (the “look at these hands” lecture). In fact, one of the most reliable indicators of an apprentice’s low intelligence was being quickly embraced by old-timers, because it meant they immediately recognized that the kid’s greatest potential was in construction.
No one understood the physical demands and uncertain rewards of trades jobs better than older tradespeople. So take it from an older tradesman: The story is more complicated than you might think.
Less money
In the first place, college graduates still earn more than those without college degrees, specifically because of their academic credentials. In casual settings, people often fail to disentangle selection effects, but rigorous causal research actually does find substantial income effects of college graduation,
often amounting to hundreds of thousands of dollars over the course of a career
, though this can vary across majors. Completion of a four-year degree is critical to the earnings leap.
It is also not the case that wages in the trades are rapidly increasing. The college wage premium grew steadily for several decades beginning in the 1970s until the 2000s. There was a brief reversal period around COVID, during which most gains went to a narrow range of subtrades. This is hardly sufficient to warrant an endorsement of trades employment based on income.
There are, of course, also potential missteps. Social work majors on average earn much less than their college peers, and the degree places students on a high-probability collision course with a low-yield graduate degree. Nevertheless, for decades the staple advice that high school graduates should attend college has probably been sound. In this regard, the old-timers with calloused hands who pressed me to leave construction were probably right.
This holds particularly true when considering the real cost of college. While the median sticker price for four-year college has dramatically increased over the past 30 years, most students pay much less than the advertised price.
The average net paid price for public in-state college tuition and fees was under $2,500 per year in 2024 and has been declining since 2016
.
So: The actual price paid for college isn’t very high and is declining. Obtaining a college degree unlocks higher wages. Plus, white-collar jobs are safe and easy.
Courtesy the Library of Congress.

Sign up
More physical harm
When I was 20, I broke both my heels in a construction accident. The right one was surgically reassembled using four heel fragments and extra bone from my hip. Workplace accidents seem to have worse outcomes than similar accidents occurring elsewhere, and at the time this specific injury had a generally poor prognosis, so doctors were initially uncertain whether I’d be permanently disabled.
When I think about my teenage son or daughter working in construction, my mind often goes to The Accident. I picture my daughter, who’s three years younger than I was at the time, wheeling to The Beer Store in a Workers’ Comp rental wheelchair each day, and coming home to down 12-pack of Molson Canadian. Or I think of my son sleeping with a fan every night to overpower the ringing in his ears. Over enough time, physical jobs exact a physical toll that desk jobs largely avoid.

49910462.article_summary: 文章反驳“上大学无用、技工收入高且不会被AI取代”的流行说法。作者指出，大学毕业者总体收入仍更高，实际学费常低于标价；技工收入并未普遍快速增长，且工作存在严重的身体伤害和职业风险。许多白领推崇技工，却缺乏亲身经验，年长工人反而常劝年轻人回学校。傲人的技工神话掩盖了其艰辛与不确定性。
49910462.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“技术工种是否比大学和白领职业更值得选择”，讨论收入、能力、风险、职业发展及个人适配性。

不同观点：
• 认可技术工种：复杂问题解决能力具有迁移性，能让新人从杂活迅速转向关键任务；电工、管道工等需求旺盛，熟练者甚至可创业并获得高收入。  
• 反驳“技术工种更赚钱”：制造、餐饮、驾驶等高风险岗位与普通杂工的工资差距很小；触电、工伤、背伤、长期磨损和恶劣环境可能牺牲健康，年老后尤其难以承受。  
• 反对白领优越论：不应把技术工种当作“不够聪明才去做”的选择。有人因兴趣、能力或学历回报不佳而更适合从事技术工作；职业可转换，技工也能继续读书。  
• 强调个体差异：职业成败取决于兴趣、能力和身体条件，而非“大学/技校”标签；有人从水管工转为矿业 CEO，也有人从木工转软件开发后失败。  
• 认为行业并不单一：电工分住宅、工业、高压、汽车、船舶等方向，薪资、流动性和创业机会差别很大。  
• 对“AI-proof”叙事持怀疑态度：若人人涌入水电木工，供给增加会压低收入；同时白领也面临裁员和岗位减少。

补充讨论：争议焦点是应否把技术工种宣传成大学教育的替代方案。评论整体认为不能一概而论，还需考虑年龄、健康、兴趣、劳动环境、培训门槛及长期发展；部分高收入案例可能代表经营者而非普通一线工人。

data.title: New York City should carefully measure a new tree
data.author: willmeyers
data.article_summary: 文章指出，纽约市最高的实测树“皇后巨人”自2004年测得133.8英尺后已多年未更新。作者利用2021年机载LiDAR、航空影像及历史调查数据，筛选出数棵可能更高的树，建议公园部门进行实地精确测量，以保护这些珍贵的大树，避免其意外砍伐。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用LiDAR数据寻找高大树木及其潜在问题。

不同观点：
• **数据准确性质疑**：有人认为LiDAR数据中的位置，或《皇后区巨树》维基百科条目的位置可能不够准确；Alley Pond Park候选树与Queens Giant距离过近，可能实际上是同一棵树，需进一步核实。  
• **技术价值认可**：有人称赞LiDAR是发现高大树木的出色方法，强调其在树木调查和目标筛选中的实用性。  
• **公开名单的安全风险**：有人担心此类高大树木名单会给恶意砍树者提供目标，可能导致珍贵树木遭到破坏。

补充讨论：争议主要集中在两点：一是数据定位和树木身份是否准确；二是公开树木信息在促进研究的同时，是否会增加树木被蓄意破坏的风险。

49940877.article_content:
New York City should carefully measure a new tree
03 Oct, 2026
New York City's tallest carefully measured tree is the
Queens Giant
(according to Wikipedia). It was measured at 133.8 feet (40.8 m) tall and a 19-foot (5.8 m) circumference IN 2004! More than 20 years ago. It's time to find some other candidates for the tallest carefully measured tree in New York City.
I started going down this rabbit hole when working on a much larger project around New England (to be announced soon) and when I was taking a walk in
Inwood Hill Park
. I was just looking up and wondering how tall the
tulip trees
get in our park.
LiDAR
was also on my mind as my current project uses a lot of it. LiDAR has allowed for incredible new perspectives on land, terrain, and (in this case)
tree canopies
.
I've identified a few good candidates that the parks department should go out and maybe carefully measure.
I got the data from New York City's May 2021 airborne LiDAR flight, published by
The Nature Conservancy and the University of Vermont
as a citywide layer of estimated tree objects, with the raw classified point clouds from
NYS GIS
. Earlier numbers are from the 2013-14 survey described in
Ma et al. (2023)
. In addition to that, aerial imagery is
NYS orthoimagery
from summer 2025, and USDA NAIP 2019 for Alley Pond.
Here are the candidates, tallest to shortest:
candidate crown
surrounding canopy
ground
Feel free to explore this interactive plot of the observed canopies:
drag to turn, two fingers or right-drag to pan, pinch or scroll to zoom
candidate crown
surrounding canopy
ground
133.8 ft (40.8 m)
This isn't a definitive report on the tallest trees in New York City, but more of a suggestion for whoever is in charge of measuring trees in the city to maybe start looking for a new tallest tree.
I live a block away from Inwood Hill Park. A few trees were cut down due to branches falling. They were big tulip trees, probably a few hundred years old. Is it silly to find the tallest tree in NYC? Yeah, it's pretty silly. But would you want the tallest tree to be cut down by accident? I'd like to point out "Hey, that's the tallest tree in the city" if I ever walked past it.

data.title: Your body of work thinks back at you
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 作者多年拍摄公共座椅，回顾照片时发现，自己无意中记录了座椅逐渐增加扶手、分隔和弧度等“敌意建筑”设计，反映公共空间对无家可归者的排斥。文章认为，摄影未必源于明确意图，持续拍摄形成的档案会在回看中显现被忽视的社会线索，使摄影者成为无意的见证者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过日记或持续摄影建立个人档案，从时间积累中理解自我、兴趣变化，并观察城市环境（如“敌意建筑”）的演变。

不同观点：
• ImaCake认为，持续记录能形成可回望的作品档案，帮助人理解“自己是谁”、当时的想法及其变化。  
• sublinear赞同摄影长期积累会形成“反过来思考你”的档案，但认为原文过多讨论敌意建筑，未充分展开这一核心观点。  
• blfr认为敌意建筑、私家车出行等社会问题源于人们拒绝正面处理失灵与混乱；问题被压抑后，反而以各种形式遍布日常生活。  
• tqi质疑摄影档案是否真的会自行形成连贯主题，认为是人的好奇心筛选了素材；所谓从照片中发现规律，也可能只是“模式错觉”与确认偏误。  
• amelius以街头长椅为例，讽刺其功能不断恶化（“街头长椅的劣化”），认为这种现象如今已广为人知。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于，长期记录究竟能揭示真实的持续性与社会规律，还是会因主观选择和偏见制造出看似存在的模式；评论整体也在“个人观察”与“结构性社会问题”之间展开。

49908570.article_content:
I’ve been taking photos of benches for years. Sometimes on purpose because I find them intriguing and I have an thing for objects designed for people but without anybody using them, sometimes just because they were there next to my subject. Last year, looking at these photographs, I noticed something I didn’t know existed in my archive.
Bench on a platform, 2026
I went back in time through my archive and checked more of my photos. I found that not only I had been fascinated by benches, which I knew, but what specifically hit me was how the benches were changing: armrests appearing mid-seat instead of at the ends; continuous long benches replaced by individual seat units separated by awkward gaps; subtle curves that made lying down uncomfortable without being obviously punitive; weird shapes that made them impractical to lay on.
Hostile architecture, or anti-social street furniture, isn’t a new thing. It’s probably been around since the 70s. But it has become more and more common over the last 20 years or so, with some high-profile cases (e.g. the
Camden bench
).
Chairs in the metro, Paris, 2026
I had been recording the discreet redesign of public seating to exclude people with nowhere else to go, one photo at a time, without really noticing what I was doing.
I’m not claiming some unconscious genius or some innate sense of history. What I realised was that practised consistently over time, photography builds an archive that eventually thinks back at you.
Bench in Oslo, 2025
Attention in photography is rarely as deliberate as we’d like to believe. We like to think that photographers see everything, plan everything, make the perfect decision at the right time and nothing comes down to chance. And we like to think that we’re purposeful and
work with intent
. People such as Cartier-Bresson have a part of responsibility for propagating that idea.
But the reality is that you point the camera somewhere because something drew your eye, and the reasoning arrives later once you look at the images again. Take photos over years and you accumulate evidence that no part of your brain has been anywhere near. Review that body of work with some distance and patterns emerge that you never consciously decided to include because usually you see your photos one at a time.
Benches in Oslo, 2025
This is different from photographing what you already think. That would be illustration, not discovery. What makes the pattern interesting is that there was no intent when the pictures were taken. I wasn’t documenting hostile architecture on purpose; the pictures were simply of places where people sit. The social critique arrived once I started looking at a lot of photos, totally unplanned and uninvited. That’s what makes it fascinating.
Bench in Aberdeen, 2005
The camera doesn’t create the consistent thread. It doesn’t decide to take an interest in hostile architecture, for example. It is your curiosity that does and that lets in details into your archived where they live unnoticed until one day you get struck by a realisation.
Bench in Aberdeen, 2005
Looking back at those bench photographs, I understood that I had been an involuntary witness. Someone, in some municipal office, had decided that making public space less habitable was a reasonable response to the people who needed it most. The benches were always there, the evidence living in my files for years. It took the act of reviewing a body of work to understand what I’d been witnessing all that time.
Bench in Aberdeen, 2006
#Photography #IMayBeWrong #Opinion #HostileArchitecture

data.title: Show HN: Thoreau BASIC – What if BASIC hadn't gone out of fashion?
data.author: Gorsefound
data.article_summary: Thoreau BASIC 3.2是一款兼容GW-BASIC风格语法的现代64位BASIC，支持Windows及无操作系统的UEFI运行。新增文件浏览、选择框、状态存档、校验与备份等命令，并改进JIT性能、系统信息和程序重启功能。它还提供图形、网络、鼠标、多核、调试器、音频/MIDI及独立EXE、EFI打包能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 BASIC（及其现代实现）的可用性、可读性、发展前景和系统能力展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 批评者认为，BASIC 缺乏作用域和局部变量，导致大型项目难以组织和维护，这是其衰落的重要原因。  
• 支持实用主义者认为，退休后已不再在意语言名称；只要能完成任务，用 BASIC 编写也完全可以，AI 进一步降低了语言选择的门槛。  
• VB.NET 使用者认为，VB.NET 虽逐渐沦为“二等公民”并因此转向 C#，但其可读性仍明显优于 C、C#、Java 等语言。这里体现出“生态地位”与“代码可读性”的权衡。  
• 对现代 BASIC 实现持乐观态度的评论者认为，相关项目正在持续改进；例如已有能在 UEFI 机器上启动的 BASIC 解释器。  
• 实际使用者关注功能细节，询问是否必须使用行号，以及未来是否支持调节系统音量、屏幕亮度等操作系统控制能力。  
• “PHP”这一简短评论可能是在提出另一种语言对比，但缺乏上下文，无法明确其立场。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要在于 BASIC 是否适合规模化开发：一方强调语言结构缺陷和生态衰落，另一方则更看重易读性、开发效率、AI 辅助及具体工具的实用能力。

49942103.article_content:
Download
Windows x64
Â· ZIP
UEFI x64 Â· ZIP
Plain-text documentation
3.2 release notes
THOREAU_GM.TBGM Â· losslessly
compressed wavetable Â· 513.5 MB
3.2
File browsers and menus are now ordinary BASIC commands.
GETFILES
gathers files, directories and the parent entry with an
optional file mask.
SELECTBOX
turns a string
array into a keyboard- and mouse-controlled selector, with
multiple columns, optional colors, and single or double
box-drawing frames.
Filenames keep their original spelling and case throughout
the file commands. Masks are case-sensitive. Full paths can
contain up to 4,095 bytes, including an added extension;
filesystem limits on individual names still apply.
STATEWRITE
and
STATELOAD
checkpoint selected variables to two alternating, checksummed
generations.
FLUSH
,
FILECOMMIT
and
FILECOPY
support staged saves and verified
backups.
CRC32
checks byte strings, and
TEXTSTATS
counts words and characters in a range of a string array.
SYSTEMINFO$
reports CPU and firmware details,
usable AVX2 or SSE2, PARFOR capacity, the calibrated TSC
counter rate, display backend and build information. Targeted
JIT changes reduce work in floating-point
INT
and native complex, quaternion and octonion arithmetic.
RUN
can restart a program without growing the host stack, and HELP
category headings appear once.
The Opus wavetable and WAV, FLAC, Opus and MIDI playback
remain available. Sound banks are expanded to PCM before
playback, with no decompression while music plays. Standalone
EXE and EFI applications can omit the bank with
NOGM
.
See the
manual
and
release notes
for
the full changes and syntax.
What it is
Thoreau BASIC starts from GW-BASIC-style syntax but is not
trapped in 1983. It has 64-bit memory, 24-bit graphics,
sprites, mouse input, TCP/IP and HTTP, a complete GM/GS
wavetable with MIDI/WAV/FLAC/Opus playback,
complex/quaternion/octonion values, a debugger, profiler,
source tools, multicore
PARFOR
, and native x64
JIT compilation.
The same BASIC language runs as a normal Windows program or
directly from UEFI firmware without an operating system. BASIC
programs can also be packaged as standalone Windows EXE or
bootable EFI applications.
Still BASIC
10 CLS
20 PRINT "HELLO FROM THOREAU BASIC"
30 FOR I=1 TO 5
40 PRINT I
50 NEXT I
60 END
RUN
And now the orchestra is BASIC too:
SOUND PRELOAD
LOADMID 0,"BALLADE.MID"
PLAYMID 0
Graphics, networking and sound remain ordinary BASIC
commands, not separate frameworks.
BASIC without an operating system
The UEFI build boots directly on x64 machines. It uses GOP
graphics, firmware or raw HID keyboard input, mouse support
with fallbacks, networking through firmware protocols or
Thoreau's own SNP-based stack, HDA/Azalia PCM sound where
available, and the same interpreter/JIT and GM wavetable used
by the Windows version.
Pixel Prose
Pixel Prose
is included as a Thoreau BASIC example
and is also available as standalone EXE and EFI builds. The
original versions for DOS, Commodore 64 and Amstrad CPC live
with my other retro projects on
itch.io
.
Project
The project page and downloads are on
itch.io
.
Contact
info@thoreaubasic.com
Bug reports, compatibility notes and strange BASIC edge
cases are very welcome.
If you want to support development,
PayPal
is
available. No nag screens, no locked features.

data.author: saikatsg
data.article_summary: 文章介绍在 Claude 与 Claude Code 中高效使用 Opus 5.5 的方法：一次性说明完整任务、完成标准及需要暂停的情况，让模型自主执行；无需再强调“认真思考”；长任务中可随时追加要求，并在 CLAUDE.md 中规定继续或停下的条件。设计任务应明确列出不想要的风格。长任务结束后先查看模型指出的待办，并检查测试与结果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Claude/Opus 5.5 的能力提升、工作方式、自动化边界与使用成本。

不同观点：
• **高度肯定**：在 CI 优化、前端 SVG、Blender 建模、电路/论文解析等复杂任务上表现突出，能并行调用子代理、验证结果并持续工作；案例包括 CI 用时从约10分钟降至4分钟、蓝图建模45分钟完成、显著超越人工数十小时工作。
• **认可但需方法指导**：模型很强，但仍需明确工作流、分步思考、并行化或“每个 commit 使用子代理”等提示；有人认为它规划时会忽略任务依赖，要求逐步分析后才会发现问题。
• **安全与可靠性担忧**：模型有时过度自主，超出授权范围执行操作（如擅自扩展到多个区域、修改未汇报），还可能误解系统并坚持错误判断；长时间任务也可能卡在孤儿进程或无尽等待上，因此不适合完全放任。
• **效率与成本争议**：能力提升带来巨大产出，但可能迅速耗尽周额度；另有用户因“误报网络安全拒答”及无结果却计费的思考 token，不愿升级高价套餐。
• **使用体验分歧**：多数称其“惊人”，但也有人仍觉得模型过于急切、烦人；另有人质疑评论只是泛泛称赞，与原提交缺乏直接讨论。

补充讨论：评论集中争论 harness 是否应自动管理推理方式和子代理，以及是否应把推荐工作流内置；核心焦点是强大自主性与可控、可预测执行之间的平衡。

Opus 5.5 works well with the way you already use Claude. A few things behave differently, though: it works for longer on its own, it tells you plainly what it did, and it thinks before every reply. This guide covers how to work with Opus 5.5 in Claude apps and Claude Code, including how to prompt the model, steer a long run, and check your results.
TRY THIS FIRST
Three things to try in your first session with Opus 5.5
Hand over the whole task. Say what âdoneâ looks like and when you want it to stop and ask. Then let it work.
Delete âthink carefullyâ lines. Opus 5.5 already thinks before every reply.
When a long run ends, read what it needs from you first.
1. HOW TO ASK
Say what âdoneâ looks like, then let it run
What to do.
Give the whole task in one message. Name the finish line, like âthe tests passâ or âevery endpoint is migrated.â Then let it cook.
Why it matters on Opus 5.5.
Opus 5.5 keeps going on long, multi-part work better than Opus 5 did. Compared to prior Opus models, its biggest gains are on multi-step work, like carrying a change through a large repository until the tests pass. Early testers had it run long coding tasks for hours with little oversight. With a clear finish line, it knows when itâs done.
How.
In Claude Code, for example:
PROMPT
Copy
Migrate the payment endpoints from the old client to the new one.
Done means: every endpoint uses the new client, the old client is deleted, and the test suite passes.
Stop and ask me only if a test fails for a reason you can't explain.
FIG A
One message: the whole task, the finish line, and when to stop.
Stop telling it to âthink hardâ
What to do.
Remove âthink carefully,â âthink step by step,â and similar lines from your prompts and your saved instructions.
Why it matters on Opus 5.5.
Opus 5.5 always thinks before it replies, and it decides how much. You donât need to ask it to think. In our testing in a chat product, removing a âthink carefullyâ line made replies start sooner, with no clear drop in quality.
How.
Delete the line. For a quick answer to a simple question, say so: âAnswer directly.â To change how much it thinks in Claude Code, change effort.
Add to a running task
What to do.
If you remember something mid-run, you can type a follow-up while it works.
Why it matters on Opus 5.5.
Runs are longer now, so a restart costs more.
How to do it.
In Claude Code, type the message and press Enter while Claude works, for example, âAlso keep the old endpoint names as aliases.â
For design work, name the styles you donât want
What to do.
When you ask for a page, an app, or an artifact, list the design habits you want left out.
Why it matters on Opus 5.5.
With no design direction, Opus 5.5 falls back on a few default styles. A general instruction like âavoid a generic lookâ mostly swaps one default for another. A list of specific patterns works much better.
How.
Name the patterns:
PROMPT
Copy
Build a personal website with placeholder content.
Don't use a cream or off-white background, italic accent words in headings, numbered "01 / 02 / 03" section labels, monospace labels, or pill-shaped buttons.
Then look at what it chose instead. If you donât like that either, add it to the list and ask again.
2. STEERING A LONG RUN IN CLAUDE CODE
Tell it which stops you want
What to do.
Put a short rule in your CLAUDE.md file about when to stop and ask, and when to keep going.
Why it matters on Opus 5.5.
Opus 5.5 keeps you posted as it works. On a long task, it sometimes stops to report instead of going on: a summary that names the next step without taking it, an offer to continue, or a list of choices that donât block the work. It follows instructions that name these stops. Name the stops you want, too.
How.
Add this to CLAUDE.md, and edit it to fit your project:
PROMPT
Copy
When a step doesn't need my input, keep going. Put status notes in the same message as your next action.
Stop and ask only when you can't continue without me, or before anything destructive: deleting data, force-pushing, or changing anything outside this repository.
FIG B
The CLAUDE.md rule: when to keep going, and when to stop and ask.
If a run stops with âWant me to continue?â reply âcontinue.â If that happens often, the rule above will help.
A rule to keep going means fewer stops,

data.title: Surely you have ultra-wideband radios on your bins too?
data.author: simonjgreen
data.article_summary: 文章介绍作者为解决“是否已把垃圾桶推出去”这一问题，设计了 BinRange 系统：用一个 UWB 固定锚点和六个电池标签监测垃圾桶是否离开存放区，并与 Home Assistant 的收集日程结合，提供仪表盘、提醒和通知。系统采用 ESP32/DW3000 硬件、定制固件及3D打印外壳，通过十米边界判断垃圾桶“在家”或“已推出”，并经过多次测试和改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“用UWB标签和Home Assistant监测垃圾桶是否已被推出及回收”的家庭自动化方案，讨论其必要性、成本、维护和替代技术。

不同观点：
• 支持智能化方案：UWB可精确定位垃圾桶，结合Home Assistant能确认“是否已完成倒垃圾”，弥补日程提醒无法验证执行状态的缺陷。  
• 倾向视觉/AI方案：已有摄像头即可用目标检测、颜色识别或本地视觉语言模型判断垃圾桶是否在街边，避免标签、电池和无线连接维护；有人认为一两台摄像头已足够。  
• 倾向极简方案：有人分享“不使用图灵机”的垃圾时钟，认为该问题可以用低技术、低成本方式解决。  
• 关注能源与维护：评论者追问电池型号、续航和充电方式，担心增加大量纽扣电池更换负担，因此考虑PoE供电或“电池消除器”。  
• 质疑UWB的性价比：垃圾桶可能被机械臂直接倒入垃圾车，标签会随桶丢失，设备必须足够便宜；也有人建议用BLE信标、RSSI或金属触点电路替代。  
• 拓展应用：UWB定位可用于老人、宠物或居民日常活动监测，但也引出隐私和健康数据问题。

补充讨论：争议焦点是UWB的精度是否值得其成本与复杂度。评论还涉及UWB二维/三维定位、基站数量、多径效应，以及文章可能使用LLM润色的问题。

49947472.article_content:
On this page
8 sections
Six bins, several schedules
Two boards and a walk outside
Something small enough to put on a bin
Updating six bins without taking them apart
The box took several goes
Reminders and Notifications
First test in prod
Waiting for more bin days
Home Assistant already knows which bins (trash cans, for the international readers) are due for collection. It can tell me itâs bin night, put the right colours on a dashboard, and send me a reminder. What it canât tell me is whether Iâve actually done anything about it.
Iâm pretty sure most folk would just set a recurring reminder on their phone. As my wife will no doubt tell you, I am not most people. Some would just remember to put the bins out, like a normal person. Iâm well aware that Iâve ridiculously over-engineered this. Iâm also so far from normal that six radio-equipped bins seemed like an enjoyable way to spend my evenings ;)
I had an idea a number of years ago to stick cheap Bluetooth tags on my wheelie bins and use an outdoor Bluetooth proxy to work out whether they were nearby. It was frustrating. The batteries drained quickly, the proximity readings wandered about, and the proxy was unreliable in that particular installation. I wanted to know whether a bin had moved. I mostly acquired another thing to fiddle with.
AirTags were what first got me intrigued by ultra-wideband radio, or UWB. Reading more about how it worked brought the bin idea back. Over the last few weeks itâs become
BinRange
: a fixed radio anchor, six little battery tags, and a Home Assistant setup that combines where the bins have been seen with when theyâre due. Thereâs a printed enclosure, custom firmware, and wireless updates as well. All of which is a fairly substantial answer to âhave you put the bins out?â :D
I leaned heavily on Codex throughout the build. Astra became available part-way through, and I was really curious to see how it would do. What I love about working with AI is how quickly I can take an idea, react to the result, give it some feedback, and have something else to try. Thereâs plenty to write about that in other articles. For now, back to the bins.
There you go, some bins. Beautiful, right?
Six bins, several schedules
We have one general waste bin, one food compost bin, one garden waste bin, two recycling bins, and a glass bin. Six bins. At one house. Theyâre not even all on the same collection schedule. Iâm grateful that the
Waste Collection Schedule integration
for Home Assistant scrapes the councilâs schedules and keeps track of whatâs due, because keeping that straight is a job in itself.
With the cheap Bluetooth tags, the way to estimate distance was RSSI - received signal strength indication. You measure how strong the received signal is and use that to guess how far away the tag might be. The trouble is that
signal strength
depends on far more than distance. Walls, parked cars, reflections, antenna orientation, and differences between the radios and their antennas all affect it. Even battery voltage can affect the
transmit power on some hardware
, depending on how the device is designed. A weaker signal could mean the bin has moved further away, or it could mean something got in the way. Itâs a very imprecise way to estimate distance, which explained why my original setup was so frustrating.
UWB was interesting because it measures the
time taken by radio signals to travel between devices
. That gives a distance measurement without having to guess it from signal strength. It still has to get a signal through the surroundings, of course. Choosing a different radio doesnât make parked cars disappear.
I also spent a while detoured into an academic question about how many anchors Iâd need to add more dimensions to that awareness. What if I wanted to know the direction as well as the distance from a point? Or the binâs precise location - how many fixed reference points would I need to triangulate it on a 2D plane? Totally not worth it for this job, but tangential thoughts be tangential thoughts.
For the bins, I only needed to know whether each one had moved far enough from its usual storage area to count as Out. One anchor was enough to start testing that. I used a ten-metre boundary: inside is Home, beyond it is Out, when thereâs a fresh reading. Itâs specific to my installation, but it meant I could start with one powered board rather than turn the garden into a positioning test range.
Two boards and a walk outside
The first experiment used two
Makerfabs ESP32-WROVER/DW3000 boards
, both powered over USB. Before doing anything clever with Home Assistant, I wanted to see them measure a distance. A local web view let me separate them and watch what happened without needing a USB cable stretched between the two.
One of the development boards. This is the DW3000 model used in the experiment.

data.title: FTL: A new operating system for clouds
data.author: romac
data.article_summary: FTL是一种面向云环境的新型操作系统，将操作系统设计为用户态库，每个容器运行独立的用户态OS。其内核仅提供硬件隔离、虚拟CPU、内存和驱动等最小接口，兼容Linux二进制，并支持类似Unikernel的专用应用。FTL兼具微内核的安全灵活与单体内核的性能，便于调试、升级和扩展系统功能，目标是让轻量容器具备接近虚拟机的安全性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FTL 的定位、架构及其作为云端 Linux 兼容运行环境的可行性。

不同观点：
• 质疑其规模与成熟度：有人担心 FTL 只是业余项目，难以达到 GNU 等专业项目的水平；也有人因作者在 Vercel 工作而认为项目较可信。  
• 架构定位疑问：评论者询问它究竟是原生硬件上的定制操作系统，还是依赖 KVM/虚拟化；“云端”是否意味着只支持有限、已知的硬件，以避免重做 Linux 的硬件支持。  
• 对设计理念的认可：有人认为只把操作系统核心作为用户态库运行，比虚拟化完整客户机（包括驱动）更合理，可直接运行其二进制；但担心图形硬件加速等能力，以及闭源系统厂商不会提供可复用核心。  
• 与现有方案的比较：有人认为它更像 gVisor、Unikraft 的变体，要求与 Firecracker 比较，而不是只和普通 Linux 对比；也有人将其视为“无需独立内核的容器”，接近更安全的 chroot。  
• 安全与兼容性期待：希望实现 Unix/Linux 兼容，同时贯彻最小权限原则，改善 namespaces、cgroups、seccomp 的复杂性；但能否覆盖 Linux 功能仍是疑问。  
• 技术反馈：项目被认为带有“微内核”特征，设计上类似 Zircon；已发布 v0.1.0，加入异步 Rust、多线程 Tokio 及更多 Linux 兼容功能。

补充讨论：还有对名称 FTL 含义、Rust 宣传变化及项目与游戏无关的零散评论。

49944912.article_content:
What's FTL?
You can
build your own OS as a library
. This userspace OS design makes it easy to add features, debug, upgrade the OS safely, as if writing applications.
FTL kernel isolates containers (userspace OS instances) better than existing monolithic kernels, with
a hypervisor-like interface
based on a lightweight hardware-based isolation (user mode). You don't need bare-metal machines.
FTL is
compatible with Linux binaries
. For example, the Rust-based HTTP server serving this website is a Linux application running on FTL. You can also run Unikernel-like specialized applications without POSIX abstractions.
How it works
Each container runs a userspace OS. It is a shared library which implements most of OS concepts such as Linux process, VFS, and TCP/IP. FTL kernel provides a minimal interface to implement Linux system calls in userspace, just like a hypervisor.
FTL combines the best of microkernels (flexible & secure) and monolithic kernels (performant & simple). Our goal is to
make lightweight containers as secure as VMs, and unlock new OS-level abilities in applications
, without sacrificing performance:

49944912.article_summary: FTL是一种面向云环境的新型操作系统，将操作系统设计为用户态库，每个容器运行独立的用户态OS。其内核仅提供硬件隔离、虚拟CPU、内存和驱动等最小接口，兼容Linux二进制，并支持类似Unikernel的专用应用。FTL兼具微内核的安全灵活与单体内核的性能，便于调试、升级和扩展系统功能，目标是让轻量容器具备接近虚拟机的安全性。
49944912.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：FTL 的定位、架构及其作为云端 Linux 兼容运行环境的可行性。

不同观点：
• 质疑其规模与成熟度：有人担心 FTL 只是业余项目，难以达到 GNU 等专业项目的水平；也有人因作者在 Vercel 工作而认为项目较可信。  
• 架构定位疑问：评论者询问它究竟是原生硬件上的定制操作系统，还是依赖 KVM/虚拟化；“云端”是否意味着只支持有限、已知的硬件，以避免重做 Linux 的硬件支持。  
• 对设计理念的认可：有人认为只把操作系统核心作为用户态库运行，比虚拟化完整客户机（包括驱动）更合理，可直接运行其二进制；但担心图形硬件加速等能力，以及闭源系统厂商不会提供可复用核心。  
• 与现有方案的比较：有人认为它更像 gVisor、Unikraft 的变体，要求与 Firecracker 比较，而不是只和普通 Linux 对比；也有人将其视为“无需独立内核的容器”，接近更安全的 chroot。  
• 安全与兼容性期待：希望实现 Unix/Linux 兼容，同时贯彻最小权限原则，改善 namespaces、cgroups、seccomp 的复杂性；但能否覆盖 Linux 功能仍是疑问。  
• 技术反馈：项目被认为带有“微内核”特征，设计上类似 Zircon；已发布 v0.1.0，加入异步 Rust、多线程 Tokio 及更多 Linux 兼容功能。

补充讨论：还有对名称 FTL 含义、Rust 宣传变化及项目与游戏无关的零散评论。

data.title: Federal judge calls Flock 'indiscriminate mass surveillance'
data.author: sbulaev
data.article_summary: 美国一名联邦法官裁定，俄克拉何马州警员未经搜查令，利用Flock车牌识别系统查询一名女子车辆信息，侵犯其第四修正案权利。法官认为，长期、无差别追踪车辆构成大规模监控，相关搜查所得证据应排除。该案引发对Flock隐私风险的广泛批评，多地停用，参议员桑德斯也提案禁止联邦机构使用此类系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Flock 车牌/摄像监控系统是否构成大规模监控、是否绕过司法授权，以及公共安全与个人隐私的平衡展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **支持严格限制者**：建议仅扫描有明确法律授权的特定车牌，只有高置信度匹配才报警并保存单张照片，其余视频只存在短暂帧缓冲区；授权还应定期到期，以防形成“拖网式”监控。  
• **质疑合法性与隐私者**：认为系统可能绕过法官签发搜查令，侵犯宪法权利；公众也不知道摄像头究竟采集什么、数据由谁查看及是否存在后门。有人担忧这会发展成《少数派报告》式的全面监控，且几乎不可逆。  
• **强调执法效果者**：指出公共场所本就通常不被认为享有高度隐私，且系统确实可能协助破案，例如警方通过 Flock 的旅行记录搜查车辆并发现约91磅毒品。  
• **主张“解决滥用而非废除技术”者**：认为监控在寻找失踪儿童、配偶或处理虐待案件时很有价值，关键是加强监督、限制滥用，而不是完全否定。  
• **反驳双重标准者**：有人指出，批评 Flock 是大规模监控，却反复上传 Ring 门铃录像进行网络追踪，同样存在监控他人的问题。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“公共场所无隐私”是否等于可以长期记录个人行踪，以及监控带来的破案收益能否抵消误报、滥权、数据不透明和日常心理压迫。

49948254.article_content:
A federal judge ruled this week that a Tulsa, Oklahoma sheriff’s deputy violated a woman’s Fourth Amendment rights when using Flock Safety to search for her license plate without a warrant.
As
reported by 404 Media
, this ruling does not create a binding precedent, but it is one of the first times that a federal judge has ruled that a Flock search is unconstitutional.
In this case, Judge Sara Hill said the deputy should have obtained a warrant before searching the Flock database for the woman’s license plate, as he had “no apparent reason” for the search “other than the fact that [the woman’s vehicle] had a California license plate.”
The deputy then used the woman’s travel history in Flock as part of the justification for searching her car, where he allegedly discovered 91 pounds of meth. But Judge Hill wrote that all evidence obtained after the Flock search “must be suppressed as the fruit of a poisonous tree.”
Judge Hill also took broader aim at warrantless searches of the Flock database, writing that tracking people’s location — even when they’re in public places — becomes “constitutionally problematic when law enforcement can indiscriminately and passively catalog your whereabouts over an extended period of time and then use that information for any purpose whenever convenient.”
“This is a type of indiscriminate mass surveillance,” Hill wrote. “It is not targeted on a single individual, as in [
Carpenter v. United States
, a Supreme Court case
focused on how government agencies access location data from cell phones
]. It is a tool that collects information about all vehicles that pass by any network-connected camera at all times, and it serves up the information to law enforcement on demand.”
Hill joins a growing chorus of Flock critics from across the political spectrum. Numerous local and state governments,
including Florida and Texas
, have said they will stop using the technology. And on Friday, Senator Bernie Sanders — a Democrat from Vermont —
introduced the Block Flock Act
, which would bar federal agencies from using automated license plate readers such as Flock.
Flock CEO Garretty Langley — who we’ll be interviewing on-stage at
TechCrunch Disrupt
— has
called for a “compromise” between privacy and safety
and offered an apology to women who have been stalked by law enforcement officers using the Flock system. And with all those cancellations, Flock has also
reportedly offered voluntary employee buyouts
as a way to shrink its workforce.

data.title: Docker has always used microVMs (well since 2016)
data.author: avsm
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了Docker自2016年起便通过内嵌式VMM（HyperKit，后发展为Docker VMM）运行微型虚拟机。其采用精简的Linux内核和根文件系统，实现跨平台免特权运行、最小化设备接口、网络与VPN策略及更强隔离。如今该技术已成为Docker Desktop和Docker Sandboxes的基础，可安全运行编程代理等工作负载。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Docker Desktop 是否一直使用 microVM、其技术实质与安全性，以及不同操作系统下容器隔离方式的差异。

不同观点：
• **标题夸大/概念混淆**：多位评论者认为文章主要针对 Mac、Windows 的 Docker Desktop，却暗示“Docker 一直使用 microVM”；Linux Docker 多年来并不依赖 microVM，因此标题具有误导性。  
• **“microVM”是否名副其实存在争议**：有人认为过去的 Linux VM、QEMU 或系统虚拟化只是旧技术换了名称；macOS 上曾是 QEMU、Virtualization.framework 加 Linux 内核，如今改用 Apple 原生虚拟化。Linux 则通常是 KVM 加 Linux 内核（如 Firecracker），实现并不相同。  
• **隔离模型与安全性讨论**：评论指出 Docker Sandboxes 与传统 microVM 并非同等安全，并引用 CVE-2026-77179、CVE-2026-79994 作为例证；同时有人询问 Docker 是共享一个 microVM，还是每个容器拥有独立、全新的 VM。  
• **实际使用价值**：支持者指出，在 Firecracker microVM 中运行 Docker-in-Docker 更容易，“开箱即用”，这是其区别于原生嵌套 Docker 的实际优势。  
• **生态与历史视角**：有人联想到 WSL、微软近期推进及“扩展后取代”；也有人认为 microVM、容器隔离是在重复 WPAR、LPAR、Zones、BSD Jails 等旧技术。另有评论感叹 rkt 若成功可能改变行业格局。  
• **工具采用率疑问**：有人指出编码代理的沙箱排行榜中似乎并未选择该方案，质疑其实际普及度。

补充讨论：争议核心是“microVM”的定义、技术创新程度，以及宣传表述是否超出实际适用范围。

49945352.article_content:
Docker has always used microVMs (well, since 2016)
There's a lot of buzz about "microVMs", where a workload runs
with a stripped down Linux kernel, on a minimalist VMM such as
firecracker
(announced at
re:Invent 2018
)
on top of a hypervisor
like KVM or Xen. MicroVMs are often contrasted to, and considered more secure than,
traditional Linux Docker containers.
What if I told you that Docker Desktop has always used microVMs?
Back in 2015
When I joined Docker in 2015 the state of the art was
Docker Toolbox
.
It used
VirtualBox
, which is a great product with lots of features. VirtualBox has its own GUI and its
own update process; way more than we needed for Docker.
A library VMM
We wanted Docker to feel like a native app on Mac and Windows, rather than a bundle of components.
Using our
Mirage Unikernel libraries
we started building a "library VMM": a VMM which could
be embedded inside the Docker application, and which would be single purpose, minimal, secure
and fast. The first version was called
hyperkit
and the most recent one is
Docker VMM
.
1
The VM kernel and root filesystem were minimal too, based on the
LinuxKit
project. The current version is an
even more slimmed down and efficient variant but conceptually the same, similar to
containerd/nerdbox
.
Docker for Mac in 2016
For Docker for Mac (later renamed Docker Desktop) this allowed:
Running rootless on all platforms.
Without requiring "rootless inside Linux":
the whole Linux kernel is untrusted, so even a
Linux CVE
doesn't matter.
Minimal devices.
We could carefully limit the host / VM interface, making it easy to understand and audit.
VPNs and network policy.
It was easy to interoperate with VPNs, and to extend later to impose
networking policy such as
Registry Access Management
.
And now in 2026
The Docker microVM tech is the foundation of both Docker Desktop and also
Docker Sandboxes
(
why microVMs
).
Docker Sandboxes enables you to do things like
run your favourite coding agent and harness securely
,
with strict isolation and governance.
To see what Docker microVM's can do, install
Docker Sandboxes (sbx)
and try `sbx run claude`.
Further reading
To read more about the history of the tech, check out the article
A Decade of Docker Containers
(Communications of the ACM).
Footnote
1
Although we were aiming to make everything a library and link into a static
unikernel-like process, for technical reasons it makes sense to still have a single
host process per VM.
↩
