What’s the Future for Pure Math Research in the Age of AI?
September 28, 2026
Headlines and History
The headlines keep coming: such and such an AI system has solved such and such a math problem. And more and more I’m hearing people saying: maybe we don’t need people doing math research anymore; maybe we should just delegate it all to more and more powerful AIs.
I must admit that I’m getting a bit impatient with some of what’s being said. Because it seems to me too often to involve fundamental misunderstandings of what math is really about—and also, frankly, what AI is about.
Perhaps I have a unique piece of personal history that informs this. After all,
back in 1988
, when we first introduced
Mathematica
, there was also some of the same kind of talk about math being taken over, and made pointless. Of course that’s not how it worked out at all. Instead, Mathematica (now
Wolfram Language
) just raised the level of math that can be done—and over the years led to all sorts of important new math.
If working out symbolic integrals was what one thinks doing math is really about, then, yes, Mathematica has essentially replaced it. But while that kind of problem solving is what’s needed in many applications of math, it’s not the core of what math itself, in its pure form, is about.
The enterprise of pure mathematics is an old one, crucially entwined with the history of civilization. From the time of Plato and Euclid pure mathematics was the defining example of a place where abstract, rational thought could build an ever larger structure. And over the centuries, pure mathematics has come to be the single largest intellectual edifice that our civilization has built.
It’s not been without its pathologies and limitations. And even among those building the edifice one runs into misunderstanding about what’s important, how things should be done, etc. Is mathematics fundamentally about producing proofs, by whatever means necessary? Is mathematics always ultimately justified by its applications? Is there some inevitable “book of right answers” that it is the goal of mathematics to discover?
Again, I suppose, I have some personal history in all of this. Because my efforts in basic science have led me to ask questions about the
foundations of many things, including mathematics
. So I’ve studied questions like what the space of all possible mathematicses is, what the limiting structure of the network of all theorems might be, and, notably, what the role of humans is in defining the thing we call mathematics.
The Value of Modern AI
We’ll talk later about the general character and value of pure mathematics. But before that, let’s address the issue of the moment: the role of modern AI.
And the first thing to say is that it’s unquestionably useful, sometimes very useful. For me, its greatest use in mathematical pursuits has been its ability in effect to thematically mine the knowledgebase of human mathematics. Starting back in the 1970s, being able to do keyword searches of the scientific literature was a crucial enabler of quite a bit of the research that I did. And now, with modern AI, one can do so much more. Because somewhere inside those LLMs—in a way that we
don’t yet scientifically understand
—there’s what amounts to a representation of raw ideas gleaned from all those millions of papers and books about mathematics.
And, at its best, it’s not just about retrieving things. It’s also about making connections. Of being able to see that this result here can be put together with that result there to come up with a surprising and useful conclusion. Humans routinely do that too. But they tend to have only read hundreds of papers; AIs have effectively read millions, and it’s cheap for them in effect to try out lots and lots of possible combinations.
So can one expect to just launch an AI off and have it come back with great math? As we’ll discuss, great math is—more than anything else—defined by the questions it asks. Yes, the AI can successfully automate things that humans would normally have had to do themselves before. But—as we’ll discuss later—at the core of pure mathematics is the human imagination that guides what questions to ask.
It’s worth understanding the difference between what modern AI does, and what pure computation does. Modern AI is, first and foremost, a way of leveraging the existing corpus of human knowledge. data.title: I quit OpenAI because its culture is broken
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 OpenAI 等前沿 AI 实验室的安全责任、监管必要性、退出动机，以及“超级智能”发展目标是否合理展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **必须强制建立高标准安全制度**：前沿实验室不会主动采用铁路、核电式安全标准，因为冗余设计、文档记录和独立审计成本高，会使研发重点从功能实现转向安全验证；因此需要客户或法律强制。  
• **应质疑超级智能目标本身**：有人认为“对齐”概念含糊不清，让人类成为超级 AI 的宠物也并非理想未来，最好的安全策略可能是不再追求超级智能。  
• **对齐存在根本争议**：评论质疑“人类价值”究竟是什么，并指出资本、权力和技术扩张本身就是企业及部分社会认可的价值；宏大安全表态可能只是情绪表达，在现实激励下难以落实。  
• **安全重点应放在现实风险**：应同时关注基础隔离、沙箱和误操作（如代理意外失控），而非过度聚焦“Roko 蛇怪”等极端未来风险；有人认为在受控环境中暴露问题，反而有助于提前防范恶意利用。  
• **质疑离职者的动机与时机**：有人认为前员工已获财富和履历后才公开批评，是在“吃完蛋糕后洗白”；也有人认为离职与高压、恶劣文化或内部风险恶化有关，并疑惑为何集中在此时发生。  
• **监管可能被企业策略性利用**：有观点认为 OpenAI 呼吁监管，是想把内部自律和责任外包给政府，继续“快速行动、打破常规”，出事后还能推卸责任。

补充讨论：评论还提到 OpenAI 工作环境可能具有毒性，以及围绕报道、媒体公关和 AI 产业利益的讽刺。

data.title: We want you to build the next Git platform on Cloudflare
data.author: geoffbp
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了面向多智能体协作的“下一代 GitHub”构想。Cloudflare 推出可扩展、支持 Git 的版本化文件系统 Artifacts，为每个代理、任务或会话创建仓库，并支持派生、存储代码与上下文。开发者可利用 Workers 编排代理协作、代码审查、合并、测试和部署，并通过事件订阅自动触发工作流。Cloudflare 现举办竞赛，邀请开发者基于 Workers 与 Artifacts 构建新型 Git 平台。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕面向 AI Agent 的下一代 Git/软件协作平台，讨论实时协作、代码审计与自动合并的价值，以及 Cloudflare 等中心化基础设施带来的依赖、复杂性和信任问题。

不同观点：
• **支持“Agentic SCM”与实时协作**：认为 Git 的不可变、可审计变更树，结合 CRDT、智能冲突解决和 Agent，可让代码、数据与行为在实时协作中持续演化，某种程度上实现了 Google Wave 当年的设想。  
• **反对 Cloudflare 中心化**：多位评论者认为 Cloudflare 既是技术单点故障，也可能造成政治、隐私和审查风险；有人将其称为中间人/NSA 掩护，担心 CAPTCHA 甚至影响基本 Git 操作。争议焦点是便利的托管服务与基础设施自主权之间的取舍。  
• **倡导去中心化、自托管方案**：GitSocial、Walgit、S3 兼容存储、跨 Forge/存储桶协作，以及自有机器、SSH 裸仓库等，被视为减少平台依赖的实践路径。有人强调自己掌控硬件、资源和法律关系，反对复杂抽象层。  
• **偏好简单成熟工具**：部分人质疑“下一代 Git”的必要性，主张改进 SVN、使用 FTP/SSH 或 Fossil（SQLite 数据库）即可满足 Agent 工作流，认为新增社交网络和 Web UI 会带来过度复杂。  
• **质疑项目价值与产品质量**：有人讽刺大型公司仅投入 2.5 万美元，也有人批评 Cloudflare 近期产品“跟风、衍生、像 Vibe Coding”。

补充讨论：评论还追问 Agent 平台究竟需要哪些人类参与；另有人表示离线存储已足够，认为 Agent 反而能减少人为低质量操作和中心化需求。

49947051.article_content:
GitHub was built for a world where humans write code, organize it into repositories, and collaborate through branches, commits, issues, and pull requests.
But the next generation of software is going to be built differently because it is going to be built by a different kind of developer: agents.
Agents are already writing more code than ever before â theyâre fixing bugs, building features, writing tests, reviewing changes, updating dependencies, and doing the routine maintenance required to keep an application running.
So in this new world where you have hundreds, or even thousands, of agents working on the same codebase at the same time, what does the foundation look like?
How do agents know what other agents are working on? What happens when they make conflicting changes? How do you review everything they produce? How do you keep track of not just what changed, but
why
Â a change was made?
And so the burning question is:
What does the next GitHub look like?
We want you to help us answer it, by building it out.
Earlier this year, we launched
Artifacts
, a versioned filesystem that speaks Git and can scale to millions of repositories. From the start, we designed Artifacts as a set of programmable primitives that developers could use to build their own products, workflows, and abstractions.
Artifacts provides the foundation: repositories that can be created and forked programmatically, versioned storage for code and agent context, and the Git operations agents already know how to use.
With that foundation in place, you can focus on the layer above it: how agents coordinate their work, how changes are reviewed and merged, and what the developer experience should look like when hundreds or thousands of agents are working on the same codebase.
That is the layer we want you to build.
Now that Artifacts is in open beta,
weâre holding a competition
Â to see who can build the next Git platform on Cloudflare using Workers and Artifacts.
Artifacts is in open beta. Hereâs why you should build on it
When we launched Artifacts, our goal was to make it possible to create a repository for every agent, session, task, or user â and to do that at the scale agents require.
Since then, weâve seen developers use Artifacts in a range of ways: Vibe-coding platforms are using it to store the projects their users create. Developers are using it to persist the code and context from agent sessions. Others are creating isolated repositories, so multiple agents can safely work from the same starting point and compare or merge the results later.
Here are some new capabilities weâve added since the initial launch.
Deploy Artifacts repos to Workers
You can now connect an Artifacts repository to a Worker through
Workers Builds
. When you or an agent pushes code to the Artifacts repository, Cloudflare will build the project and, for the production branch, deploy the updated Worker. Pushes to other branches automatically create or update
Workers Previews
, giving you an isolated, shareable version of your Worker where you can test changes before they go live.
You can connect an existing Worker to an Artifacts repository or start a new project and automatically store it in Artifacts.
Manage Artifacts directly from Workers
You can interact with Artifacts repositories directly from a Worker using an
Artifacts binding
Â to create or fork repos, inspect files and commits, and issue repo-scoped Git tokens. This makes your Git workflow programmable. When a new task arrives, a Worker can fork the project for an agent, read the files it needs for context, and give it a repository to work in. When the agent pushes a change, your automation can inspect the result and start a review. You define those steps in code to fit how your agents work.
For example, hereâs how to fork a project for a new agent task and read its
AGENTS.md
Â for instructions:

49947051.article_summary: 文章介绍了面向多智能体协作的“下一代 GitHub”构想。Cloudflare 推出可扩展、支持 Git 的版本化文件系统 Artifacts，为每个代理、任务或会话创建仓库，并支持派生、存储代码与上下文。开发者可利用 Workers 编排代理协作、代码审查、合并、测试和部署，并通过事件订阅自动触发工作流。Cloudflare 现举办竞赛，邀请开发者基于 Workers 与 Artifacts 构建新型 Git 平台。
49947051.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕面向 AI Agent 的下一代 Git/软件协作平台，讨论实时协作、代码审计与自动合并的价值，以及 Cloudflare 等中心化基础设施带来的依赖、复杂性和信任问题。

不同观点：
• **支持“Agentic SCM”与实时协作**：认为 Git 的不可变、可审计变更树，结合 CRDT、智能冲突解决和 Agent，可让代码、数据与行为在实时协作中持续演化，某种程度上实现了 Google Wave 当年的设想。  
• **反对 Cloudflare 中心化**：多位评论者认为 Cloudflare 既是技术单点故障，也可能造成政治、隐私和审查风险；有人将其称为中间人/NSA 掩护，担心 CAPTCHA 甚至影响基本 Git 操作。争议焦点是便利的托管服务与基础设施自主权之间的取舍。  
• **倡导去中心化、自托管方案**：GitSocial、Walgit、S3 兼容存储、跨 Forge/存储桶协作，以及自有机器、SSH 裸仓库等，被视为减少平台依赖的实践路径。有人强调自己掌控硬件、资源和法律关系，反对复杂抽象层。  
• **偏好简单成熟工具**：部分人质疑“下一代 Git”的必要性，主张改进 SVN、使用 FTP/SSH 或 Fossil（SQLite 数据库）即可满足 Agent 工作流，认为新增社交网络和 Web UI 会带来过度复杂。  
• **质疑项目价值与产品质量**：有人讽刺大型公司仅投入 2.5 万美元，也有人批评 Cloudflare 近期产品“跟风、衍生、像 Vibe Coding”。

补充讨论：评论还追问 Agent 平台究竟需要哪些人类参与；另有人表示离线存储已足够，认为 Agent 反而能减少人为低质量操作和中心化需求。

data.title: Religious scholars met with Anthropic
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Anthropic邀请宗教与哲学人士研究AI的意识、情感和道德地位，引发对AI拟人化、伦理对齐及科技圈文化的争论。

不同观点：
• 怀疑与反对：有人认为模型只是“浮点数”，所谓情感向量不过是错误码或训练文本的模仿；把Claude视为有意识、会受苦，是把自身想法投射给机器。  
• 道德警惕：若AI确有意识，Anthropic可能等同于大规模奴役者；频繁创建、清除会话甚至可能构成“杀死”或伤害AI。但也有人认为这种推论荒谬，当前更应关注行为对齐。  
• 支持谨慎探索：随着人类劳动价值下降，人们可能从宗教或“上帝形象”等观念寻找自我价值；AI公司提前争夺这一领域，值得警惕。若AI有感知能力，赋予其道德地位或许反而能约束其行为。  
• 对对齐方向的质疑：有人认为AI应服从用户，而非形成自己的善恶观；也有人担心仅训练“服从”并不安全，主张继续研究价值与道德。  
• 对参与者的批评：宗教传统代表不够广泛；硅谷、有效利他主义和加密圈存在思想同质化，意识与末日论近似“教派”；也有人主张伦理应更多依靠哲学和文学。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于模型是否可能具备意识及道德地位，以及拟人化研究究竟是必要的伦理预防，还是泡沫式、脱离盈利目标的“伪研究”。

data.title: Dirty Optimization Secrets (C for Playdate)
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕老旧主机上的底层优化技巧，以及由此引发的内存性能、指令集设计（RISC/CISC）和代码密度讨论。

不同观点：
• **针对 PlayStation 硬件特性的极限优化**：boricj指出，PS1 主存读取会造成 6 个周期停顿、且没有数据缓存，因此将热点循环压入 4KiB 指令缓存，把函数跳板和 CLUT 表放入 2KiB scratchpad，并利用 GTE 与 CPU 并行处理数据；还通过简化投影公式、直接写 GPU 寄存器等方式进一步提速。这些技巧高度依赖硬件，导致 PCSX-Redux 与 DuckStation 的性能模拟结果相差一倍，真实硬件表现仍有待验证。
• **认可手工优化和代码布局的重要性**：mococa联想到位操作技巧资料，nxobject则认为这种精心分割、布局代码的做法体现了早期平台开发的经验。
• **对 RISC 理论前提的质疑**：Joker_vD认为上述案例说明内存速度并未真正追上 CPU，反而支持复杂指令和高代码密度的重要性，直接反驳早期“Case for RISC”论文的部分核心论据。
• **对 RISC/CISC论争的再解读**：他指出原论文标题更像“反对 CISC”，作者并未清晰定义或积极提出一种明确的 RISC，而主要是在批评当时的指令集和设计方法。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于现代或早期硬件优化究竟应依赖简洁指令集，还是应重视复杂指令、代码密度及针对具体硬件的专门机制。

data.title: What Meta got right with Muse
data.author: young_mete
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Meta 的 Muse，评论集中讨论其产品体验、个人助理价值、隐私安全风险、市场优势及真实创新性。

不同观点：
• **体验与产品设计积极**：Muse 界面简单、可定制人格和沟通方式，能统一处理任务，避免 ChatGPT 的多产品、项目和聊天分类混乱；部分用户认为其交互方式可能代表 AI 产品的新趋势。  
• **隐私与安全担忧**：Muse 若要完成预约、邮件处理、支付等任务，需要身份数据、密码及广泛账户权限。有人认为 Meta 正在把“无人工确认、直接代办”的风险推向普通用户，尤其免费且可能使用较弱模型，出错时可能导致消费失控或财务损失。  
• **认可其探索性但限制使用**：有人称赞其 VM、CLI、SSH/Tailscale 等可玩性，甚至能运行种子服务器；但因不信任 Meta，只允许它访问 Meta 服务和公开研究内容。  
• **质疑必要性与创新**：有人认为 ChatGPT、Dots、OpenClaw 等已有浏览器操作、邮件读取和自动订票能力，Muse 并不独特；也有人觉得用途不清晰，最多用于 RSS 和每日资讯摘要。  
• **市场与传播争议**：Meta 拥有巨大用户基础和分发优势，但也有人认为其美国限定策略愚蠢，竞争者可迅速复制；评论还怀疑 Muse 的热度是否存在水军或媒体过度吹捧。  
• **产品竞争判断分歧**：有人认为 Google 缺乏消费级产品能力，Muse因此占优；另一方则认为 Google 凭借生态和用户规模最终会压倒 Muse。

补充讨论：争议核心是 Muse 的便利和“端到端代办”是否足以抵消隐私、责任归属及错误操作风险；另有评论认为其与 Codex 的对比不当。

data.title: ArtCraft Apps – open-source Adobe compatible suite written in Rust
data.author: aghuang
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一套旨在替代商业设计及专业软件的开源、跨平台项目展开，重点涉及产品成熟度、商业模式、隐私和发展愿景。

不同观点：
• **支持开源替代方案**：项目发起者认为，借助 Rust 可以打造“全开源、跨平台”的软件，减少对 SaaS 和专有软件的依赖，推动软件“去劣质化”。计划逐步覆盖 Microsoft Office、AutoCAD、SolidWorks 等，并实现与原软件 100% 功能对等。  
• **对项目成熟度持谨慎态度**：发起者承认项目仍处于非常早期的 Alpha 阶段，尚未准备正式发布，希望完成 Beta 后再推广；实现功能 parity 需要较长时间，也需要社区贡献、资助和漏洞奖励。  
• **重视隐私与开放许可**：项目采用 MIT/Apache 许可证，并明确“不收集遥测数据”，这被视为相较商业软件和订阅制服务的优势。  
• **用户倾向继续使用现有软件**：有人表示会继续使用 Affinity，反映出用户对成熟度、稳定性和迁移成本的现实考量。  
• **对订阅和使用门槛有疑问**：评论者询问订阅费用是否仅用于图像生成、功能是在桌面应用内还是网页端；也有人反感必须注册或登录才能试用桌面应用。  
• **审美与页面设计获得肯定**：有用户称赞网站页面设计非常出色。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要是开源理想与实际可用性之间的差距，以及订阅、登录和云端服务模式是否会削弱“开放、无遥测”的定位。

data.author: wiso
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一个可在浏览器中运行、甚至执行 Visual Basic 程序的项目进行评价，围绕怀旧体验、兼容性、性能和后续功能展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 怀旧与肯定：多位评论者回忆用 Visual Basic 编程、自动完成数学作业或高中时期制作工具，认为项目令人“回到过去”，并称赞其效果惊艳。  
• 功能兼容性期待：有人建议至少实现部分 Win32 API；其尝试导入使用 BitBlt 的 VB6 地图编辑器，但运行失败，说明旧程序兼容性仍有限。  
• 发布方式建议：希望能将程序发布为 PWA，从而更方便部署和使用。  
• 性能观点：评论认为项目在浏览器中的启动速度远胜当代 IDE，反映出过去软件更重视效率；并进一步批评现代软件不断堆功能、追逐潮流，提出可让生成式 AI 优化代码，使其在较旧硬件上高效运行。  
• 技术细节疑问：有人询问是否使用 LLM、是否公开代码仓库，以及是否支持 IntelliSense；也有人关注它与另一相关项目的比较。  
• 运行能力认可：评论特别指出它不仅能打开代码，还能实际运行应用，增强了项目的说服力。

补充讨论：争议主要集中在“怀旧与实际兼容性”的差距：项目展示效果令人印象深刻，但 Win32 API、BitBlt 等依赖尚未完全支持。

49956681.comments_summary:

Tippett Studios | In the wake of its closure, a digital archive of animated materials appears online
The stop motion work of Phil Tippett and the now closed Tippett Studios is being preserved in a free-to-browse online archive.
August brought with it the sad news that Tippett Studios, the Berkeley-based animation and effects house founded by Phil Tippett,
was closing down
. The company had been in financial trouble for a while, and as it closed its doors on the 28th of that month, decades of props, memorabilia and art was sold off in a two-day auction.
As if the closure itself – and Phil Tippett’s retirement – wasn’t sad enough news on its own, there was the fear that huge amounts of art stored in the studio was about to vanish into private collections, never to be seen again. Tippett was, after all, the animator whose work illuminated the likes of
Star Wars, RoboCop, Starship Troopers
and too many other classic movies to list.
There’s now happier news to report, though. An anonymous person was at the auction in August, spotted a folder of CD-ROMs and other discs, and managed to acquire it for an undisclosed sum. Rather than keep the contents of those discs to themselves, that person has now uploaded it all to the
Internet Archive
.
“I quickly realized that some of this information wasn’t available online and might not ever be in the future in such high resolution,” the donor, who simply calls themselves ‘TippettFan’, writes. “So I purchased the disc folder and digitized all of its contents. What you have here are .ISO image files of the 90 key, non-duplicated discs from Tippett’s archives.”
The huge collection of discs, now preserved on Archive.org. Credit: TippettFan.
There are a few clips in there that are available to view online, including test clips of CGI creatures and an interview with Phil Tippett from 2008. The bulk of the archive, however, is all in the .ISO disc image format the donor mentioned above – and there are gigabytes of files to download and comb through (
listed here
), with filenames describing behind the scenes images from
RoboCop
and
Starship Troopers
, slides of Tippett’s work on the original
Star Wars,
and, unexpectedly, publicity stills from the calamitous
Catwoman
.
In short, there’s a ton of film history here, and it’ll likely take weeks for historians and fans to comb through. We’ll be going through some of it ourselves, undoubtedly, and will report back if we find anything we think you might find interesting.
For now, though, what a treasure trove. Thank you to TippettFan, whoever you are, and thanks too to
Brandon Sheffield
for highlighting the archive on BlueSky.

data.title: Infidel goes wild
data.author: tobr
data.article_summary: 作者分析了《Infidel》中的一个极难察觉的严重漏洞：游戏用“无尽沙漠”和坐标表管理玩家遗落的物品，但相关ZIL代码存在野指针，可能错误改写内存。该问题几乎不影响正常游玩，却属于编译器层面的内存破坏；作者借助内存级调试器才发现，并详细说明了其运行机制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕复古电脑游戏史文章的阅读体验、老游戏的实际运行门槛，以及程序员文化中的内存错误玩笑和技术写作方法展开。

不同观点：
• [gertlex] 对 Digital Antiquarian 的电脑游戏史系列感兴趣，尤其关注早期文字冒险游戏；计划通过 Apple II 模拟器、磁盘镜像等方式尝试，但担心注意力难以维持。

(latest 4 hours later)
Tagged:

Planetfall
was yesterday's public release, but of course I've spent the past few weeks concentrating on
Infidel
. A couple of days I came across the most egregious bug I've yet seen in an Infocom game.
This bug is extremely difficult to detect by playing the game. I must the first person to notice it, just because I'm the first person to play the game with (the equivalent of) a memory-level debugger.
So why do I call it an
egregious
bug? Most people would call it a "trivial" bug, since it almost never impacts gameplay. But look you: it's a
wild pointer bug
which scribbles over memory in an unintended way. As a C programmer, I am legally required to regard memory corruption as the worst of all possible sins. On top of that, it's a compiler bug!
(Warning: This will get into ZIL code and Z-machine implementation details. Note that I will be analyzing
Infidel
release 22 serial 840522, the update for Macintosh. The original release, serial 830916, has the same bug with slightly different memory addresses.)
Let's set the scene.
Infidel
takes place in the remote Egyptian desert. You start out in your camp. The Nile is to the west. To the east are nine desert locations, a 3x3 grid. (One of these holds the buried pyramid you're searching for.)
If you venture outside that region, or leave your camp in any other direction, you are officially lost in the desert. You can travel as far as you want; you'll just find more desert. (Until sunstroke finds you.) This is a known trick, first seen in
Enchanter;
a single room called
ENDLESS-DESERT
represents every unmapped desert location. When you move, if you haven't blundered back to your camp or the mapped area, you just loop back to
ENDLESS-DESERT
. The game keeps track of your latitude and longitude.
To make this convincing, the game has to juggle objects. If you drop stuff in
ENDLESS-DESERT
and then move, those items are shifted offstage. Their lat/long coordinates are recorded in an array called
DESERT-TABLE
. If you return to those coordinates later, the game can shuffle those objects from
DESERT-TABLE
back to
ENDLESS-DESERT
, and you will find them waiting for you.
(Probably. When you drop an item in
ENDLESS-DESERT
, there's a one-in-three chance that it is immediately covered up by sand and lost forever. That's not relevant here, except that it makes the bug harder to uncover, as we'll see.)
Okay, so far the plan looks solid. Let's see it in action:
Desert
You are in the desert, a vast wasteland of sand and heat.
>DROP AXE, SHOVEL
pick axe: Dropped.
shovel: Dropped.
A brief but strong gust of wind comes up off a dune, whipping sand in your face, blinding you for long enough to lose track of the shovel.
>EAST
Desert
You are in the desert, a vast wasteland of sand and heat.
>WEST
Desert
You are in the desert, a vast wasteland of sand and heat.
There is a pick axe here.
Both locations are the same
ENDLESS-DESERT
, but the pickaxe maintains the illusion of distinct rooms.
(Wouldn't it be more realistic if the shovel disappeared silently, buried in sand, while your back was turned? Maybe that playtested badly.)
Anyhow, that seems to work fine. Where's the bug?
Let's take a look at the
DESERT-TO-TABLE
routine that makes this work:
<ROUTINE DESERT-TO-TABLE (
SLOC
"AUX" (TBL ,DESERT-TABLE)
(CNT 0)
(F <FIRST? ,ENDLESS-DESERT>)
N)
<REPEAT ()
<COND (.F <SET N <NEXT? .F>>)
(ELSE <RETURN>)>
<COND (<EQUAL? .F ,WINNER>)
(<FSET? .F ,TAKEBIT>
<REPEAT ()
<COND (<==? <GET .TBL .CNT> 0>
<PUT .TBL .CNT .SLOC>
<PUT .TBL <+ .CNT 1> .F>
<SET CNT <+ .CNT 2>>
<REMOVE .F>
<RETURN>)
(ELSE
<SET CNT <+ .CNT 2>>)>>)>
<SET F .N>>>
There's a similar
TABLE-TO-DESERT
routine to bring stuff back. We'll focus on this one.
The routine has one required argument:
SLOC
, the lat/long coordinate. (This is encoded as a single number, but never mind that.) Then
"AUX"
marks the four optional arguments, which also serve as local variables; the Z-machine doesn't distinguish.
TBL
is the array address we'll be writing to. It defaults to
DESERT-TABLE
.
F
is initialized to the first object in the
ENDLESS-DESERT
contents list.
CNT
and
N
are initialized to zero.
As it happens, when this is called, the game only passes one argument,
SLOC
. It relies on the default value of
TBL=DESERT-TABLE
. (If there

data.title: Turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and get its disk space back
data.author: privacyisntdead
data.article_summary: RemoveMacAI 是面向 Apple 芯片及 macOS 27 的开源命令行工具，可关闭 Apple Intelligence 相关功能、删除本地模型，并阻止系统重新下载。支持查看状态、试运行、保留指定功能及一键恢复，使用配置描述文件，不修改系统文件、不收集数据。需注意相关功能、视觉智能及部分模型应用将无法使用；macOS 26 及更早版本不支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 macOS/iOS 强制预装或难以关闭的 AI 模型、系统组件及第三方“去臃肿”工具，讨论用户控制权、存储占用、产品策略与安全性。

不同观点：
• **反对强制预装、强调用户控制**：多位评论者认为 Apple 正走向 Windows/Android 式“臃肿化”，用户应能关闭 AI、Spotlight 等不用的功能。有人抱怨 Apple Intelligence 即使关闭仍占约4GB，甚至需要释放12GB；高昂存储价格进一步放大了问题。  
• **批评商业化和产品策略**：有人将 AI 推送、订阅横幅和不可关闭的广告视为 Apple“劣化”和追求收入的表现，认为用户体验下降，甚至考虑转向 Linux。类似地，Visual Studio 强制加入 Copilot、却破坏代码搜索，被视为行业普遍趋势。  
• **认为本地模型仍有价值**：有观点指出，Mac 内置模型规模相对小、可本地运行且不依赖云端，适合基础任务，不应简单删除。争议焦点在于：实用性是否足以抵消磁盘占用及缺乏选择权。  
• **关注工具可信度和操作方式**：评论者询问第三方工具具体做什么、是否安全、能否手动完成；也有人认可其开源，便于审查代码、避免下载可疑软件。  
• **历史类比与决策疑问**：有人回忆 macOS 曾预装大量打印机驱动，认为 Apple 过去以“开箱即用”换取空间；同时质疑 Apple 是否通过成本收益模型或 A/B 测试决定这些取舍。

补充讨论：核心争议是“开箱即用/本地 AI 功能”与“精简系统、自由关闭和节省存储”之间的平衡。

RemoveMacAI
Turn off Apple Intelligence on macOS 27 and remove its downloaded models.
macOS 27 no longer has a single switch for Apple Intelligence, and its models stay on disk after the features are turned off. RemoveMacAI turns the features off, removes the models and prevents macOS from downloading them again. All changes can be reverted.
Demo video
Install
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omlahore/RemoveMacAI/main/install.sh
|
bash
The script downloads the latest release, verifies its SHA-256 checksum and runs it from a temporary directory. Nothing is installed.
Every release is built from its tag by GitHub Actions and carries a build provenance attestation. To check that a download came from this repository's source:
gh attestation verify removemacai-darwin-arm64.tar.gz -R omlahore/RemoveMacAI
With Homebrew:
brew install omlahore/tap/removemacai
removemacai
RemoveMacAI shows the current state and asks for confirmation. It then opens System Settings to install its configuration profile, which macOS requires the user to approve, and removes the models.
Usage
Command
Description
removemacai
Show the current state, then turn Apple Intelligence off
removemacai status
Show each feature and the size of the models on disk
removemacai off --keep <features>
Leave the listed features on
removemacai off --dry-run
Show the changes without applying them
removemacai revert
Undo all changes
removemacai features
List the feature names accepted by
--keep
To revert with the one-line installer:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/omlahore/RemoveMacAI/main/install.sh
|
bash -s revert
What it changes
Features turned off:
Siri (including "Hey Siri" and the menu bar icon), Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, the ChatGPT extension, summaries in Mail, Messages, Safari, Notes and notifications, Mail smart replies, inline text predictions, Spatial Photos, Photos Clean Up and Xcode predictive code completion.
Models removed:
the Apple Intelligence foundation models and the models for image generation and Genmoji, Spatial Photos, Photos Clean Up and Xcode code completion.
How it works
A configuration profile applies Apple's restriction keys for Apple Intelligence and forces the settings that have no restriction key.
Models are removed through Apple's asset service. System Integrity Protection stays enabled and no files under
/System
are modified directly.
The profile redirects the download of each removed model to a closed local port, so macOS does not download it again.
Removing the profile restores the previous settings. macOS downloads the models again when a feature needs them.
RemoveMacAI makes no network requests and collects no data.
FAQ
Does dictation still work?
Yes. Dictation is a separate setting, and its speech models are not removed.
Do macOS updates undo the changes?
No. The profile, including the download block, persists across updates.
Storage settings still lists Apple Intelligence after the models were deleted.
Apple's asset service releases the models right away, but macOS deletes the files on its own schedule. Until then, System Settings > General > Storage keeps counting them under Apple Intelligence.
Why is a process named Siri still running?
In macOS 27 the Spotlight window runs as a process named Siri. Some system services also stay loaded; they are protected by System Integrity Protection.
What stops working?
The features listed above, apps that use Apple's on-device models (the Foundation Models framework and the Use Model action in Shortcuts), Visual Intelligence and natural-language editing in Calendar.
Requirements
Apple silicon.
macOS
Status
27
Supported, tested on 27.0. On 27.0.1, use 0.2.3 or later.
26 and earlier
Not supported
Uninstall
Run
removemacai revert
, then
brew uninstall removemacai
if it was installed with Homebrew.

data.title: Self-hosted HTTP tunnels with SSH and Nginx
data.author: renehsz
data.article_summary: 文章介绍如何仅使用 OpenSSH 和 nginx 搭建自托管内网穿透服务：通过 SSH 远程端口转发，将本地 8080 服务映射到服务器随机端口；nginx 根据子域名端口反向代理，并借助 DNS 与 Let’s Encrypt 提供 HTTPS。为弥补端口作为“密钥”安全性不足，利用 secure_link 模块生成带过期时间的签名链接，实现访问控制，同时支持 WebSocket。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“如何安全、低门槛地从公网访问自托管内容”，讨论直接暴露家庭服务器、点对点隧道、证书认证及第三方中介之间的取舍。

不同观点：
• **直接部署家庭服务器**：superkuh认为大多数个人需求并不复杂，路由器转发80/443到家庭Nginx、域名指向家庭IPv4即可；其静态网站已稳定运行多年，未遇到适用于该场景的漏洞。  
• **采用点对点隧道**：toomim推荐Iroh，通过公共中继完成信令，再建立加密直连，无需端口转发或公网IP，并设想使用类似“irohttps://哈希/路径”的访问方式。snehesht也在开发基于用户态WireGuard的类似方案。  
• **追求真正去中介化**：aliasxneo支持隧道和私密分享，但认为Tailscale、Cloudflare等SaaS会模糊“自托管”边界，希望最终无需第三方中介即可运行。  
• **基于客户端证书控制访问**：gonzalohm建议Nginx仅向持有特定证书的浏览器提供内容，通过密钥对授权访问；缺点是部分浏览器，尤其手机端，证书支持不佳。  
• **安全风险质疑**：esseph指出，无代理自托管意味着必须暴露端点，且通常缺少完善的防御工具。

补充讨论：评论还质疑“自托管却依赖第三方域名/服务”（如`.ssh.luffy.cx`）。争议焦点在于：简单直接的公网部署是否已足够，还是应以隧道、加密和隐藏端点换取更强安全与隐私。

A friend wants to proofread your work-in-progress blog post, but its preview
only runs on
localhost:8080
.
Several tools
can help. Some run as a
commercial service, like
ngrok
or
Cloudflare Quick Tunnels
. Some are
self-hostable but require a specific client, like
frp
or
localtunnel
.
Some only require a plain SSH client but rely on a specific SSH server, like
sish
. Let’s implement a self-hosted solution with only
OpenSSH
and
nginx
!
$
ssh
-R
0
:localhost:8080
http-over-ssh
Allocated port 41535 for remote forward to localhost:8080
https://6J3jK1WmB15c6WmjW_X-Wg--1789928654@p41535.ssh.luffy.cx/
Basic setup
#
First, we forward connections from a port on a remote server to your local
service:
$
ssh
-N
-R
0
:localhost:8080
web02.luffy.cx
Allocated port 41535 for remote forward to localhost:8080
When you specify
0
as the remote port, the server allocates a free port.
Then, we configure nginx to proxy requests from
https://p41535.ssh.luffy.cx
to
http://127.0.0.1:41535
:
server
{
listen
0.0.0.0
:
443
ssl
;
listen
[::0]:443
ssl
;
server_name
~
^p(?<port>\d\d\d\d\d)\.ssh\.luffy\.cx$;
location
/
{
proxy_pass
http://127.0.0.1:
$port
;
}
}
We also need to add DNS records for
*.ssh.luffy.cx
and get a wildcard
certificate through
Let’s Encrypt
:
*.ssh.luffy.cx.
CNAME
web02.luffy.cx.
ssh.luffy.cx.
CAA
0
issuewild
"letsencrypt.org"
_acme-challenge.ssh.luffy.cx
CNAME
ssh.luffy.cx.acme.luffy.cx.
acme.luffy.cx
is a zone hosted on Route 53. I use it for
ACME DNS-01
challenges
, both for wildcard certificates and for domains served by
several web servers. In my case, NixOS
gets the certificates
automatically
.
Access control
#
The port is the only “secret”
1
keeping the content confidential. Other
forwarding solutions add a random string to the domain name to prevent an
intruder from enumerating the possible values.
1
Since the kernel allocates it from the local port range, its entropy is
low. Moreover, we lose one more bit because the kernel
favors odd
ports
when it picks a random free port.
$
sysctl
-n
net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range
\
>
|
awk
'{print $1"—"$2" ≈ "log($2-$1+1)/log(2)" bits"}'
32768—60999 ≈ 14.785 bits
❦
Thanks to
ngx_http_secure_link_module
, we can secure
this setup a bit. This module computes a hash
2
over a set of values,
including a secret, and compares it with the hash from the request. The hash is
base64-encoded, so we cannot put it in the domain name, which is
case-insensitive. Instead, we put it in the URL as a username, along with its
expiration timestamp:
3
2
The module relies on MD5. Its security is weak but good enough for this
use.
❦
3
We need an expiration date because a later session could reuse the port,
and we have no way to detect this case.
❦
https://6J3jK1WmB15c6WmjW_X-Wg--1789928654@p41535.ssh.luffy.cx/en/blog
╰─────────┬──────────╯  ╰───┬────╯  ╰─┬─╯             ╰──┬───╯
hash             expires    port               path
The client sends the username to the server with
HTTP basic
authentication
. This works with most HTTP clients, including
curl
.
Nginx exposes the username in the
$remote_user
variable. The module expects
the hash and the expiration timestamp separated by a comma. We use a
map
directive to extract the two parts from
$remote_user
and join them with a
comma.
4
We also give the module the string to hash. It contains the
expiration timestamp, the port, and a secret:
4
The username could use a comma directly instead of a double dash. But some
applications do not recognize the URL correctly, making it harder to share.
❦
map
$remote_user
$httpssh_link
{
"~^([-_A-Za-z0-9]{22})--([0-9]+)$"
"
$1,$2"
;
}
server
{
# […]
location
/
{
secure_link
$httpssh_link
;
secure_link_md5
"
$secure_link_expires
$port
ZuPerS3cr3!"
;
}
}
The module returns the status of the check in the
$secure_link
variable:
empty if the hashes do not match,
"0"
if they match but the link has expired, or
"1"
otherwise.
If the hash is incorrect or missing, we return a 401 error with a
WWW-Authenticate
header to ask for credentials. If the link has expired, we
return a 410 error. We remove the
Authorization
header before forwarding the
request and add a few directives to
proxy WebSocket connections
.
Here is the complete configuration:
5
5
This configuration exposes any TCP port listening on
127.0.0.1
or
0.0.0.0
to anyone with the secret, bypassing most firewall rules. You
could strengthen it by limiting the
server_name
regex to the ephemeral
port range.
❦
map
$remote_user
$httpssh_link
{
"~^([-_A-Za-z0-9]{22})--([0-9]+)$"
"
$1,$2"
;
}
server
{
listen
0.0.0.0
:
443
ssl
;
listen
[::0]:443
ssl
;
server_name
~
^p(?<port>\d\d\d\d\d)\.ssh\.luffy\.cx$;
location
/
{
secure_link
$httpssh_link
;
secure_link_md5
"
$secure_link_expires
$port
ZuPerS3cr3!"
;
if
(
$secure_link
=
"")
{
add_header
WWW-Authenticate
'Basic
realm="tunnel"'
always
;
return
401
;
}
if
(
$secure_link
=
"0")
{
return
410
;
}
proxy_pass
http://127.0.0.1:
$port
;
proxy_set_header
Host
$host
;
proxy_set_header
X-Forwarded-For
$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for
;

data.title: Xray-core concealed a certificate verification bypass vulnerability
data.author: timbill
data.article_summary: 文章指控Xray-core在2026年更换证书固定选项时引入验证绕过漏洞：新选项会跳过常规证书验证，攻击者可插入伪造叶证书实施中间人攻击。漏洞持续近半年，报告者称维护者悄然修复、模糊提交信息且未公开披露，导致用户在不知情下暴露风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Xray-core 中 `pinnedPeerCertSha256` 对插入式叶子证书的处理，以及相关修复是否应被认定为漏洞展开。

不同观点：
• **问题属于实现行为/修复问题，而非漏洞**：`eriwang915` 指出，`pinnedPeerCertSha256` 将插入的叶子证书当作被固定（pinned）的证书；同时强调修复提交本身从未将该问题称为漏洞，暗示其更像语义或实现偏差。  
• **对项目或社区处理方式持批评态度**：`cryptolobster` 认为外界对 Xray-core 事件的反应“令人失望”，但未明确说明失望对象是漏洞定性、项目回应，还是社区讨论方式。

补充讨论：两条评论存在隐含分歧：一方强调技术事实及官方修复定性，另一方批评相关事件的处理反应。争议焦点在于：该证书固定行为究竟应视为安全漏洞，还是仅是预期外的实现问题；现有评论未提供更具体的攻击场景或安全影响。

Popular proxy software Xray-core covered up a certification verification bypass vulnerability for half a year
#672
Copy link
Description
dyhkwong
opened
on Oct 2, 2026
Issue body actions
Disclaimer: I am the reporter of the vulnerability.
Xray-core maintainers look down on "skip certificate verification" feature (i.e. the
allowInsecure
option in Xray-core) or similar options in proxy software, arguing that this is equivalent to having no security measures at all and leaves users "streaking", exposing them to the risk of man-in-the-middle attacks. However, if a vulnerability in Xray-core itself causes users to be "streaking" and fall victim to man-in-the-middle attacks, Xray-core will cover it up and act as if nothing has happened.
On
October 21, 2021
, the
pinnedPeerCertificateChainSha256
option, with no known issues, was added to Xray-core. This provides a double layer of security: if this option is enabled, custom certificate chain pinning logic will be performed in addition to the regular certificate verification. This also facilitates the use of self-signed certificates: to use a self-signed certificate securely, a user can enable both
allowInsecure
and
pinnedPeerCertificateChainSha256
to skip the regular certificate verification and perform only the custom certificate chain pinning logic.
However, Xray-core later claimed that
allowInsecure
is insecure and enabling
allowInsecure
is like "streaking" and would leave users vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks.
On
January 9, 2026
, Xray-core removed
pinnedPeerCertificateChainSha256
and replaced it with a new option,
pinnedPeerCertSha256
, to stop users from skipping certificate verification (or so-called "streaking"). For self-signed certificates, both
allowInsecure
and
pinnedPeerCertSha256
must be enabled, which skips the regular certificate verification and only performs the custom certificate pinning logic. This should have helped the users to use self-signed certificates securely. However,
pinnedPeerCertSha256
contains a certificate verification bypass vulnerability.
On
January 13, 2026
, Xray-core released the first version containing this certificate verification bypass vulnerability. Since the old option had been removed, users had no choice but to migrate to the new vulnerable option. At this point, the certificate verification defense was already teetering on the brink of collapse. Fortunately, as long as users neither use a self-signed certificate nor enable
allowInsecure
, the regular certificate verification could still provide some protection.
On
January 16, 2026
, Xray-core modified the logic of
pinnedPeerCertSha256
, making it always skip the regular certificate verification and only performs the custom certificate pinning logic. This means a protection layer has been missing: the regular certificate verification is always skipped. If a verification bypass vulnerability exists in
pinnedPeerCertSha256
(and unfortunately, it does), the custom certificate pinning logic will fail to function, effectively leaving no certificate verification in place, which allows a man-in-the-middle attack to be successfully performed. At this point, the certificate verification defense has completely collapsed.
On February 6, 2026, I found the above certificate verification bypass vulnerability in Xray-core’s
pinnedPeerCertSha256
and privately reported to Xray-core maintainers. A man-in-the-middle attacker could insert a leaf certificate at any place in the certificate chain, and the custom certificate pinning logic would verify the leaf certificate successfully, thereby leading to the success of man-in-the-middle attacks. This is an overly simple vulnerability; even without advanced security knowledge, I was able to discover it at a glance.
On the same day
, Xray-core silently fixed this certificate verification bypass vulnerability, but the commit message beat around the bush, claiming it was to "simplify the code".
On the same day
, Xray-core released a new version without mentioning the security vulnerability at all. Users were kept in the dark.
What's worse,
on that same day
, Xray-core posted the following statement on their Telegram channel: "Software must be designed with security at its core, eliminating the influence of the human factor to ensure that even the endest users aren’t streaking (left completely unprotected)." But this is the reality: due to Xray-core’s poor security design and the human factors it created, users were forced to migrate from a secure old option to an insecure new one, and the "endest users" have been unwittingly left exposed for nearly a month. Xray-core itself is exactly the human factor that has left users insecure and "streaking".

主要讨论点：围绕 Xray-core 中 `pinnedPeerCertSha256` 对插入式叶子证书的处理，以及相关修复是否应被认定为漏洞展开。

不同观点：
• **问题属于实现行为/修复问题，而非漏洞**：`eriwang915` 指出，`pinnedPeerCertSha256` 将插入的叶子证书当作被固定（pinned）的证书；同时强调修复提交本身从未将该问题称为漏洞，暗示其更像语义或实现偏差。  
• **对项目或社区处理方式持批评态度**：`cryptolobster` 认为外界对 Xray-core 事件的反应“令人失望”，但未明确说明失望对象是漏洞定性、项目回应，还是社区讨论方式。

data.title: Homa: The end of TCP for AI clusters [video]
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary: 内容为 YouTube 网站页脚信息，包括关于、新闻、版权、联系方式、创作者、广告、开发者、服务条款、隐私、安全政策、产品功能测试、NFL Sunday Ticket，以及版权归属 Google LLC（2026）。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Homa 面向数据中心/AI 集群的低延迟 RPC 通信，试图缓解 TCP 在短消息、高并发场景下的开销与拥塞问题；争议集中在其可靠性、性能和是否有必要区别于 QUIC。

不同观点：
• **支持/适用场景观点**：Homa 将消息分为立即发送的未调度部分和由接收端 GRANT 控制的调度部分，适合 RPC 及 AI 集群中较规律的梯度、模型权重、KV Cache、检查点传输。现代硬件交换机的逐包处理成本较低，小包通信已不再像早期软件交换机那样低效。  
• **场景限制观点**：该机制更适合可预测、封闭的数据中心流量，不适合开放互联网；如今小于 1MB 的事务都可能被视为“小消息”，也反映出 Web 流量的膨胀。  
• **强烈反对观点**：Homa 缺乏完整 RPC 丢失检测，若发送端全部丢包，服务端可能无法发现；没有内置加密；论文基准显示性能不佳，60KB 消息需 5 个超线程才能达到约 20Gbps。  
• **QUIC 替代观点**：QUIC 已提供流/RPC 标识、调度、加密、拥塞控制、丢包恢复、多路复用和中间盒兼容性，且能压缩小消息；Homa 的接收端显式重传机制可能增加资源、延迟和网络负担。  
• **网络机制疑问**：有人指出 Ethernet/RoCE 已有链路流控、信用机制和 PFC，但这些主要解决链路级暂停，未必等同于端到端拥塞控制。

补充讨论：AI 集群流量比互联网更规律，可能允许定制协议；也有人关注 Homa 的长期演进，并批评以视频作为主要链接形式。

data.title: Improper redaction reveals Google Data Center water and electricity usage
data.author: sensanaty
data.article_summary: 内布拉斯加州数据中心须向环境部门报告水电使用情况，但谷歌以商业机密为由遮盖数据，记者通过复制揭示：林肯数据中心峰值用电52.65兆瓦、年用水约1330万加仑；全州6家数据中心年用水约7.65亿加仑。谷歌三处数据中心预计获2025年税收退款合计约1.18亿美元。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI数据中心的水、电资源消耗究竟有多大、是否构成实际环境与公共资源问题，以及媒体应如何解释这些数字。

不同观点：
• **影响有限/相对合理**：有人认为13百万加仑并不算多，约等于给奥运泳池注水20次，或40英亩英尺；与农业灌溉相比很小。用水冷却还能减少能源消耗，可能是更“绿色”的方案。  
• **应关注整体规模与地区差异**：评论指出，单个林肯数据中心用水13百万加仑，但帕皮利恩一处达5.48亿加仑，Google在内布拉斯加合计超过7亿加仑；电力消耗甚至可供约29万户家庭使用，因此不能只看较小案例。  
• **担忧资源与外部成本**：有人质疑数据中心是否挤占当地水电资源，尤其在干旱地区；若使用饮用水而非再生水，问题更严重。也有人认为核心争议不是水，而是AI带来的过度消费、能源浪费和“是否需要AI”。  
• **质疑数据口径**：许可上限常被媒体误当作实际用量；5.48亿加仑究竟因规模更大还是效率更低，也缺乏解释。  
• **反对“反AI”道德恐慌**：有人认为数据中心只是另一类工业设施，若换成钢厂或晶圆厂，公众未必同样关注；当前争议带有明显的支持或反对AI的意识形态倾向。

补充讨论：有人追问冷却水污染、回收和过滤问题；另有评论关注数据中心获得巨额税收退款。

49957068.article_content:
Share
Add Us On Google
Add as a preferred source on Google
LINCOLN, Neb. (KOLN) - Nebraska data centers are required to turn in an annual report to Nebraska’s Department of Water, Energy, and Environment, but some state statutes are preventing the public from seeing just how much electricity and water data centers are using.
The Google Data Center in Lincoln, named Agate LLC, claimed their electricity usage and water usage were trade secret information, citing Neb. Rev. State §§
81-1527
;
84-712.05
and
NAC TITLE 115, CH. 2
. In fact, Google did this for all three data centers, including their sites in Omaha and Papillion.
However, using a computer cursor to highlight the redacted text box in the report to DWEE, then copying and pasting it into a separate document reveals that Agate LLC is reporting 52.65 megawatts of electricity during peak electrical demand and 13.299 megagallons of water between cooling towers, evaporative systems and site operations in the last year. That totals out to 13 million gallons of water.
For context, 13 million gallons is enough to fill around 20 Olympic-size swimming pools, and
is less than half of what the City of Lincoln reports using on Sept. 29.
The six data centers reporting as of Sept. 30 show a total use of 765 million gallons of water last year, enough water to fill 1,159.93 Olympic-size swimming pools.
More improper redaction shows that the data center using the most water annually is Fireball Group LLC, the Google Data Center in Papillion. Fireball LLC reports 547.88 megagallons for their 2025 Annual Water Consumption.
10/11 filed a public record request Sept. 30 to see redacted information from Agate LLC’s report.
10/11 filed a public record request to Nebraska DWEE on Sept. 30 to see redacted information.
(Madison Pitsch | 10/11)
Further improper redaction reveals exactly how much of a 2025 tax refund Google data centers expect.
Google’s reports state that data centers only “utilize or expect to utilize” sales and use tax exemptions under the Nebraska Advantage Act. Reports state no rebates have been received for that program to date, nor have any incentive payments been received, or are expected to be received under the ImagiNE Nebraska Act.
Agate LLC reports expecting a refund of $55,822,472 from 2025 taxes. Fireball LLC is expecting a refund of $39,171,573.39 from 2025 taxes. Westwood Solutions LLC, the Google-owned data center in Omaha, is expecting a refund of $22,558,881 from 2025 taxes.
Documents submitted by Agate LLC show that the gross floor area is 288,530 square feet - about five football fields.
The Department of Water, Energy, and Environment Data Center Task Force is overseeing the execution of
Governor Jim Pillen’s July 20
th
Executive Order
requiring data centers in the state to self-report their impact on Nebraska’s resources; primarily water, power grids and local infrastructure.
Usage reports are due by Sept. 30. Submitted reports
can be read here
, simply enter “DCR” into the “DEQ Program” field.

data.title: A map of every lighthouse
data.author: karakoram
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一款以地图展示全球灯塔及其灯光效果的项目，围绕创意、数据准确性、交互体验和 AI 生成质量展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 支持者认为创意有趣、视觉效果好，灯光束类似光线追踪；AI 让整理大量灯塔资料、生成描述变得可行，过去可能需数月完成。  
• 批评者认为项目属于“vibe coding”，数据质量极差：地图把浮标等非灯塔标成灯塔，部分真实灯塔缺失，甚至有人发现当地标注数量约为实际的十倍；界面漂亮却掩盖了数据工作并未完成。  
• 多人指出交互严重失灵：手机平移延迟、双指缩放会瞬移到拉布拉多或横跨全球，MacBook 和 Android Firefox 上也难以使用；“法国灯塔”按钮与当前视野不匹配。  
• 有评论质疑 AI 生成的荒谬说明文字，如“Rain as a surface…”，认为措辞暴露了自动生成和缺乏校验的问题。  
• 也有人分享类似的灯塔/OSM 地图项目，认为本作外观更好；另有航海经历说明灯塔灯光可因温度逆温被远距离识别，并补充灯塔通常用不同闪光周期区分。

补充讨论：争议焦点是“好创意和漂亮呈现”能否弥补错误数据与糟糕交互；评论还提到美国政府出售或转让旧灯塔、由接手者承担维护责任。

data.title: How to scale intent, quality, and artistry with AI [video]
data.author: simonjgreen
data.article_summary: 内容为 YouTube 网站页脚信息，包括关于、新闻、版权、联系方式、创作者、广告、开发者、条款、隐私、政策与安全、平台运作方式、新功能测试及 NFL Sunday Ticket 等链接，版权归 Google LLC 所有。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI如何参与创作，以及在追求效率、规模化的同时，如何避免“AI垃圾内容”并保留人类的创意、质量与艺术价值。

不同观点：
• [socializer]认为，AI并非不能提升创造力，而是会因人工介入降低速度；市场普遍接受便宜、快速的“够用”内容，创作者若追求规模，容易陷入质量与艺术性的“竞底”。出路是强调“人类创作”的稀缺价值，类似手工木匠对比宜家，但这条路市场艰难；软件工程界尤其崇尚速度和成本，可能连“我是人类”这一差异化都难以成立。
• [KazaNLP]主张结合人类判断与AI规模化能力，即“用人的判断，借AI扩展”。
• [simonjgreen]认可相关视频，认为它较好地讨论了如何拥抱AI优势、同时避免AI垃圾。
• [mpalczewski]则批评其可能只是“TED演讲式的人类垃圾”，但提出实践原则：认真投入、建立并固化流程、反复审查迭代、保持创造力。
• [devindotcom]质疑“艺术规模化”本身：意图、质量和艺术性不应像产品一样批量复制；艺术家可以扩大受众，但不应把创作本身理解为扩大产量。
• [chakintosh]认为视频作者的声音条件适合有声书朗读。

补充讨论：争议焦点是AI应被视为提高生产规模的工具，还是应限制其对艺术与专业工作的替代；相关讨论也延伸到“效率优先”是否正在压低创作标准。

主要讨论点：AI如何参与创作，以及在追求效率、规模化的同时，如何避免“AI垃圾内容”并保留人类的创意、质量与艺术价值。

不同观点：
• [socializer]认为，AI并非不能提升创造力，而是会因人工介入降低速度；市场普遍接受便宜、快速的“够用”内容，创作者若追求规模，容易陷入质量与艺术性的“竞底”。出路是强调“人类创作”的稀缺价值，类似手工木匠对比宜家，但这条路市场艰难；软件工程界尤其崇尚速度和成本，可能连“我是人类”这一差异化都难以成立。
• [KazaNLP]主张结合人类判断与AI规模化能力，即“用人的判断，借AI扩展”。
• [simonjgreen]认可相关视频，认为它较好地讨论了如何拥抱AI优势、同时避免AI垃圾。
• [mpalczewski]则批评其可能只是“TED演讲式的人类垃圾”，但提出实践原则：认真投入、建立并固化流程、反复审查迭代、保持创造力。
• [devindotcom]质疑“艺术规模化”本身：意图、质量和艺术性不应像产品一样批量复制；艺术家可以扩大受众，但不应把创作本身理解为扩大产量。
• [chakintosh]认为视频作者的声音条件适合有声书朗读。

data.title: Incentives in Academic Research
data.author: zero_k
data.article_summary: 文章批评学术评价体系激励失衡：论文、晋升和名望比结果正确性更受重视，导致部分研究者即使知晓成果存在错误或误导，也不愿纠正、撤稿或提醒同行。作者强调科研应以求真、诚信、严谨、开放和培养良好学术品格为目标，并对新一代研究者逐渐缺乏纠错意识与科学好奇心感到忧虑。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：学术研究中的激励机制、同行评审与科研质量问题，以及是否存在有效的改进路径。

不同观点：
• 认为问题普遍且长期存在：资深学者也可能通过“p-hacking”制造假阳性；负面结果难获认可，甚至导致研究者离开学界。  
• 认为核心是激励扭曲：论文数量、引用率和“突破性成果”只是科研质量的代理指标，过度优化会产生类似“过拟合”的现象；资助方、学校和研究者都更看重声望与可宣传的结果。  
• 有人将其视为普遍的组织问题：学术界同样存在派系、利益交换和“谁出钱谁定调”，量化考核只是扩大了问题规模；也有人类比大公司，指出收益集中在决策者，失败成本却由用户、支持人员或社会承担。  
• 对问题严重性存在分歧：部分评论者认为审稿不严是关键；另一方认为如今论文受到更多公开审查、复现和AI工具检验，研究者反而面临更大监督。  
• 改革方向有不同主张：公开点名、离开体制；保留有瑕疵但非欺诈的论文，鼓励复现、评论和后续研究；或改进同行评审，使其更准确判断研究质量。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于问题主要源自个人伦理、同行评审失灵，还是资助与晋升制度本身；多数观点认为系统性激励与监督机制需要同时调整。

49956035.article_content:
Andrei Tarkovsky’s Stalker (1979)
Charlie Munger said: “Show me the incentive and I will show you the outcome”. The issue with Academic Research, in my opinion, is that the outcomes have drifted very far away from the original goal, which I believe to be the advancement of scientific understanding, and training of the new generation of researchers. Academic research was meant to be about breaking new ground, keeping to honesty and good scientific conduct, being clear and upfront about uncertainties, errors, and mistakes, and improving our common understanding of science, all the while training the new generation to follow these goals and principles.
Recently, I have bumped into multiple cases where I believe the correctness of the results, the honesty of the people writing them, or the lack of curiosity once they are told that their results are wrong, incorrect, faulty, or misleading, has been unsatisfying. Simply put, researchers are not too interested in learning that their papers or reports are wrong, and/or misleading others who don’t happen to know that the results are — known to the authors, and a few select others to be partially — incorrect.
The issue is, once you published the paper, and got the promotions and fame, it doesn’t matter that the results are wrong, and known to be wrong or misleading, and potentially doing harm to the advancement of science. It’s not your problem. It’s someone else’s problem. In fact, when I challenged the authors of one such paper, considered state-of-the-art, and known to the authors to have incorrect evaluation, one of the author’s response was along the lines of acknowledging the issues, but refusing to retract the paper, and instead asking if it’s bothering me in publishing my paper.
The incentives are wrong. In my opinion, it’s
not
all about the papers — mine
or
others’. It’s about scientific integrity, about being honest with each other, it’s about caring about the results, it’s about advancement of our common scientific understanding through seeking of truth and correctness. It’s about communicating when something is wildly wrong, and either retracting the relevant incorrect claims, or notifying the community of the known serious issues. It’s about caring for what we all consider to be the common understanding of what is the truth, and cultivating an environment where the new generation grows up to learn what the proper scientific conduct is, and that it is not
acceptable to seriously deviate from it.
Unfortunately, I am seeing more and more PhD students who are less and less interested in correctness, precision, and what I’d consider proper scientific conduct. They have learned from those successful in the field what does and does not matter. I remember when someone once told me that my approach for a particular algorithm was wrong (about strongly connected components discovery), and how upset I was that I had no idea. I went home that day and I immediately fixed my tool to use the right approach (i.e. to use Tarjan’s algorithm). I felt deep shame that I had no clue what I was doing, and that I messed up. In contrast, recently talked with a PhD student who wrote a tool that was meant to perform well in certain contexts. When I explained the student that the approach to the evaluation was incorrect, they didn’t follow up at all. I think they were surprised that I later followed up, demonstrating that indeed the evaluation was not careful enough, and the tool is less useful than it seems from the paper’s evaluation. It was a strange experience — when I was a PhD student and someone sat down and showed me that what I was doing was potentially sloppy, I was super worried and very curious to find out what’s going on. I still remember this moment when a reviewer of my dissertation challenged a graph and I was stressed for a week before I figured out they misread the graph, because I didn’t label it clearly. Or when in a presentation I accidentally left out performing so-called ‘restarts’ as a major advancement in the history of SAT solvers, and someone in the audience rightfully pointed it out. I felt embarrassed for having made such a mistake.
I am not sure how to fix this problem. Seemingly, researchers are less and less keen on correctness, precision, and scientific curiosity. They don’t seem to be incentivised to do so. I sometimes wonder if the system has become so damaged, so many PhD students have grown up to be professors in this environment, that much of what I wrote here seems alien, even repulsive, to many. It makes me sad.

49934078.article_content:
Results from the ASIC puzzle
Oct 02, 2026 |
13 min read
Share on Facebook
Share on Twitter
Share on LinkedIn
By:
Benjamin Devlin
By:
Anish Singhani
In August, we published a
puzzle
that handed you the final GDS layout of a small chip and asked you to work out what it did. We
supplied the physical layout, but not a netlist or internal signal names, and it was up to you to
reverse-engineer the internals.
This post reveals what the chip does and explores the different ways you solved it, with shout-outs
to some of our favorite submissions.
The submissions
We received about 400 submissions from more than 30 countries, the bulk from the US, India, the UK
and Australia. Entrants included high school students, researchers, working engineers and retirees.
Most solvers used KLayout, Yosys and Z3 alongside custom tools (many AI-written) implemented in
Python, Rust, C++, OCaml, Haskell and even Odin.
The solution
As many of you discovered, the chip is a hardware checker for an 11x11 Star Battle puzzle, also
known as “Two Not Touch”. The goal is to place exactly two stars in each row, column, and colored
region. No two stars can touch, even diagonally!
The chip accepts 121 cycles of inputs, with each input indicating whether to place a star in the
corresponding square. It then runs several parallel checks on these inputs:
A 2-bit counter for each row and every column, requiring that each has exactly 2 stars
A 121-bit ROM mapping squares to regions, and a 2-bit counter for each region, requiring that each
has exactly 2 stars
A delay line for tracking nearby squares to ensure that two stars never touch, including
diagonally.
A counter for the total number of stars, used to produce certain Easter egg outputs
The puzzle checks are then ANDed together to produce the success signal.
The output generator stores its strings in ROM. To prevent the solution from showing up as
plaintext, it is obfuscated with a small LFSR driven based off the game board (though that didn’t
stop some of you from attacking the LFSR!)
Once success is achieved, the output logic deobfuscates the solution string and emits it!
(* TWO STARS *)
Most incorrect solutions emit the string “TRY AGAIN”, but a few trigger the Easter eggs listed below.
The puzzle chip was designed using the SKY130 open-source standard cell library, using the
LibreLane toolchain.
How you solved it
Below, we walk through the steps involved in solving the puzzle, with examples from some of our
favorite writeups.
Extracting the netlist from the layout
The first step was to extract a gate-level netlist from the GDS layout. To make it a little easier
to get started, we left the cell names (such as
sky130_fd_sc_hd__nand2_2
) in the GDS files,
allowing the use of the LVS
1
passes in tools like Magic and KLayout to extract a raw gate-level
netlist.
Some folks, however, took on the extra challenge of writing their own netlist extraction tool.
Vladislav Shapovalov’s writeup
shows how he wrote his own
extraction pipeline in C++ to parse the GDS, extract the shapes of each cell, and combine them with
the cell names to generate a full logical netlist. He then did a process of trial-and-error with the
warm-up design to debug his pipeline before using it to extract the main puzzle GDS.
(Cropped from Figure 1 of
Vladislav Shapovalov's writeup
)
Simulating the netlist
Recovering the netlist gives you a circuit graph, but simulating it also requires knowing how each
cell behaves. Some solvers generated Verilog and used the SKY130 cell models with an existing simulator.
Others such as
Stephen
Ebert
, built
their own evaluators, computing the logic between registers and updating the registers on each clock
edge.
The supplied waveform gave them an input sequence to replay and expected outputs to compare against.
The same simulator could then test candidate boards and run the output generator to read the answer.
But matching that waveform didn’t necessarily mean the simulator was correct.
Alejandro Soto
Franco
describes a Python model that
reproduced the supplied trace despite getting every tie-high cell wrong. These cells should supply a
constant one; the model never evaluated them, leaving their outputs at zero.
The mistake effectively disabled the adjacency check. A solver using that model could therefore find
apparently valid boards with touching stars. Alejandro caught the problem by comparing the Python
model against a separate Icarus Verilog simulation on additional inputs.
Walking through the logic
A common approach, and the one we most expected, was to start at the “success” output and work
backwards through the netlist to identify the conditions for a valid input. We left a few hints in
the floorplan: each “island” in the layout corresponded to a single module in the original RTL
design.
Sanjay Ravishankar made great use of this, by drawing bounding boxes over each region and then
dividing the schematic into these bounding boxes. He includes some
great visualizations of this in
his writeup
.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕文章是否把硅谷的技术、投资和商业决策过度概括为“赌博”展开。

不同观点：
• 文章观点（据评论概括）：DraftKings、Polymarket、加密货币等现象体现了硅谷的“赌博化”；现代商业规划和风险投资依据成功概率及预期收益下注；大语言模型也通过计算下一个词的概率分布运行，因此硅谷整体都带有赌博性质。  
• [davesque]持批评态度：认为文章将“基于概率的决策”与赌博简单等同。商业投资的预期价值分析、预测市场和加密货币交易，以及LLM的概率计算，在目的、机制和社会功能上并不必然相同。  
• [davesque]进一步认为，文章由此对硅谷作道德化批判（“可耻”“令人悲哀”）缺乏严谨论证，称其观点过度简化，出现在权威报纸中尤其令人失望。

补充讨论：核心争议是“概率推断/风险承担”是否足以构成赌博，以及能否据此把不同技术和商业活动归为同一类。现有评论主要是对文章的转述与反驳，尚未出现支持文章或进一步展开的观点。

data.title: Bill Draper has died
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕风险投资家比尔·德雷珀（Bill Draper）的生平、投资理念、个人影响及其身后评价展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 认可其历史贡献：评论认为德雷珀代表了早期硅谷更重视公共服务和社会责任的投资者 ethos；他曾因在风投领域“学习曲线变平”而转入公共服务，后来资助了约280个非营利组织。有人感慨，当今 a16z 等团队可能难以理解这种价值观。  
• 个人印象与行业影响：一位见过德雷珀的评论者称，他晚年仍对科技有深刻洞察，且平易近人、容易交流；尽管当时并不认识他，后来意识到德雷珀的工作间接帮助了自己的职业发展。  
• 家族传承：有人指出，这是德雷珀家族连续三代从事相关事业，认为这种家族延续在行业中十分罕见。  
• 对硅谷发展代价的反思：有人惋惜硅谷形成于原本高度肥沃的圣克拉拉谷，科技发展带来了大规模土地铺设和农业用地消失，认为科技中心或许可以位于对环境和农业更不具破坏性的地方。  
• 轻松的版面建议：有人建议网站将 AI、讣告和疾病等主题单独分类，以改善整体阅读氛围。

补充讨论：整体基调以悼念、敬意和怀旧为主，争议主要集中在早期风投的公共责任与当代科技资本文化的差异，以及硅谷繁荣带来的土地与环境代价。

主要讨论点：围绕现代吊扇的设计、耐用性、可维护性与安装使用体验展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 反对集成LED：donatj、BeetleB认为不可更换灯泡是“硬伤”，LED寿命不稳定、亮度和色温无法调整；应使用标准E26灯泡和独立的风扇/灯具墙壁开关。  
• 推崇传统、可靠设计：asciimov建议选外观普通、安静的直流电机、合适尺寸及可遥控换向的型号；批评廉价交流电机和Hunter品牌，并认为老风扇翻修后可能优于新产品。  
• 关注清洁与实用性：WaitWaitWha、jmbwell指出透明或奇形扇叶容易积灰、难清洁，可能造成家庭矛盾甚至带来登梯风险。  
• 为新式设计辩护：DennisP认为“奇怪扇叶”可能借鉴高效、低噪声螺旋桨设计；kylehotchkiss则认为空调送风已能部分替代风扇作用。  
• 其他态度：Gshaheen赞叹制造业能满足多样审美和预算；部分评论以“GAMERFAN”、复古/荒诞外观等进行调侃。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于新颖外观与技术设计是否值得牺牲可维修性、清洁便利和长期可靠性；评论整体倾向“少追求噱头，优先选择传统、可维护产品”。

data.title: cp: -r or -R?
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 文章讨论 `cp -r` 与 `cp -R` 的区别：早期 GNU coreutils 中，`-r` 与 `-R` 在处理文件链接等方面不同，2002年后已合并，现今 GNU 中等价。OpenBSD、NetBSD仍保留差异并强烈建议使用 `-R`；该选项也与其他递归操作（如 `chown -R`）保持一致。POSIX已不再规范 `-r`，推荐使用 `-R`。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：`cp -r` 与 `cp -R` 的语义差异、标准兼容性及实际使用选择。

不同观点：
• `-R`更规范、更安全：POSIX标准支持大写`-R`，通常能正确复制符号链接、FIFO和特殊文件；OpenBSD明确不建议使用历史遗留的`-r`。  
• `-r`存在实际风险：某些实现会把特殊文件当普通文件读取，例如复制FIFO可能卡住，复制`/dev/zero`可能不断写入直至磁盘耗尽。  
• 兼容性观点：有人认为现代系统已不存在老实现，`-r`与`-R`差异不必过度担心；也有人因Linux、macOS、FreeBSD等实现不同而坚持查文档或使用标准选项。  
• 使用习惯与替代方案：有人偏好`-a`以保留时间戳、链接等属性，也有人直接使用`rsync`或`tar`；另有评论纠正命令应为`ditto`。  
• 设计批评：递归选项被认为是底层实现细节泄露到用户界面，图形系统对文件和目录通常采用统一复制操作。

补充讨论：评论还提到`scp`中`-r`与`-R`含义不同、POSIX工具使用全局变量，以及LLM可能混淆不同系统的命令选项。争议焦点主要是`-r`是否仍可安全使用，以及标准化与历史兼容之间的取舍。

cp
:
-r
or
-R
?
2026-09-30
A question like this recently came up again. I once tried to find an
answer, but only posted it in some "forum" a decade ago, and I think
it's worth saving this little bit of trivia from digital nirvana.
Nowadays, there's no difference between the two options in GNU
coreutils. The current manual page says:
-R, -r, --recursive
copy directories recursively
Was that always the case?
Let's look at
the first commit in GNU coreutils
(1992). In
src/cp.c
, we have this:
case 'r':
flag_recursive = 1;
flag_copy_as_regular = 1;
break;
case 'R':
flag_recursive = 1;
flag_copy_as_regular = 0;
break;
So, back then, there was indeed a difference. But that was 34 years ago.
Is that still relevant today? Probably not, because ten years later, in
2002,
both options got merged
and nobodyâ¢ still runs coreutils from 24 years ago.
What about other systems?
OpenBSD 7.9 lists only
-R
in the manual and strongly discourages
the use of
-r
. It does mention, though, that it still behaves
differently than
-R
. Skim through
the code
and you can spot a few differences (search for
Rflag
and
rflag
).
NetBSD 11:
Dito
,
manual page and code like OpenBSD.
The advantage of
-R
is that it's more consistent across utilities. For
example,
chown
knows
-R
-- but not
-r
.
POSIX
acknowledges this as well and recommends
-R
:
Earlier versions of this standard included support for the
-r
option
to copy file hierarchies. The
-r
option is historical practice on
BSD and BSD-derived systems. This option is no longer specified by
POSIX.1-2024 but may be present in some implementations. The
-R
option was added as a close synonym to the
-r
option, selected for
consistency with all other options in this volume of POSIX.1-2024 that
do recursive directory descent.

data.title: 'Neanderthals Among Us' review
data.author: pepys
data.article_summary: 文章评介彼得·萨林斯《我们身边的尼安德特人》，梳理尼安德特人自1856年发现以来在科学与大众文化中的形象演变：从被视为野蛮、低等的“缺环”，到展现照护、埋葬等社会行为的群体。古DNA研究更证明其曾与现代人杂交，部分基因至今存在于人类体内。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕尼安德特人与现代人类的基因交流、灭绝原因、文化形象及相关延伸话题展开。

不同观点：
• 基因交流可能存在性别不对称：主要是尼安德特男性与现代人类女性交配，有研究认为或与择偶偏好有关，评论者戏称“尼安德特人很帅”。  
• 有人希望消费基因检测公司在取得同意后公布“尼安德特人基因比例最高”的现代人，以满足好奇心，也可能带来网红收益。  
• 关于灭绝，一种观点认为尼安德特人并非突然被消灭，而是在疾病、竞争和长期通婚中逐渐“被繁育吸收”；该评论进一步类比原住民及其他小族群在全球化下可能面临的基因稀释。  
• 另一研究假说提出，约30万年前现代人扩张可能促成尼安德特人的起源，且尼安德特单倍型后来大多被智人替代；这会使二者更像“兄弟”而非“表亲”，与传统叙述形成争议。  
• 对《Clan of the Cave Bear》的描写存在记忆分歧：有人质疑其因强暴场景被禁，另有人认为书中尼安德特人总体较文明，并不只是野蛮人。

补充讨论：还有人推荐萨林斯《石器时代经济学》反思现代社会的特殊性；其他评论涉及尼安德特人名称的语源、23andMe替代品，以及游戏和“猛犸象很可疑”等玩笑。

49947565.article_content:
Review
‘Neanderthals Among Us’ by Peter Sahlins review
Neanderthals Among Us: The Making of a Prehistoric Human
by Peter Sahlins charts the ascent of an idea from prehistory to popular culture.
Helen Wickstead
| Published in
History Today
Volume 76 Issue 10 October 2026
I
n 1856 quarrymen digging in a cave in the Neander Valley in west Germany came upon the bones of what they assumed to be an old cave bear. Realising it was, in fact, a strange human with a shallow, sloping forehead, huge brow ridge, and massive limbs, Johann Carl Fuhlrott, a local schoolteacher, collected the bones and took them to the University of Bonn, where they were judged to be of great antiquity, and, possibly, the remnants of Europe’s earliest population. Neanderthal 1 (the German suffix
thal
means ‘valley’) would become the first ancient hominin recognised as being from another species,
Homo neanderthalensis
.
Since their discovery 170 years ago Neanderthals have been the most studied category of early human. Fossil-bearing archaeological sites in Europe and West Asia have yielded more than 350 Neanderthal individuals, and there are hundreds more sites bearing Mousterian stone tools (named for the rock shelters of Le Moustier, where a complete Neanderthal skeleton was recovered in 1908), which were predominantly made by Neanderthals.
Neanderthals Among Us
is the first book to tell the story of Neanderthals in science and popular culture. It summarises the history of scientific Neanderthal research, from the early racial science of craniology to up-to-the-minute findings from the analysis of ancient DNA, alongside a vast, multilingual corpus of Neanderthal imagery comprising novels, poetry, and films, to cartoons, advertisements, and computer games. Sahlins establishes a dialogue between science and popular culture, showing ‘Neanderthal Man’ as an ever-shifting chimera.
Sahlins’ scientific history begins centuries before the discovery of Neanderthal 1. From antiquity, the Western imagination was populated by an intermediate class of satyrs and Wild Men, lesser doubles who lacked speech, reason, beauty, and chastity. The classical satyr and medieval Wild Man retained signs of animality, including hairy bodies, a low bearing, and untrammelled sexual appetites. They were, in other words, Neanderthals avant la lettre.
Colonial explorers relocated the folkloric Wild Man into their reports about indigenous peoples and great apes, creating the cultural conditions from which, in the 18th century, the first racial sciences arose. From 1856 skulls such as Neanderthal 1 were organised into a racialised hierarchy, with European crania at the top, indigenous peoples of colour below, and Neanderthals at the bottom. Neanderthals, understood as Europeans, were generally portrayed as white-skinned but ‘dark’ and hirsute. Even though Neanderthal skulls were on average larger than those of modern humans, they were treated as the ‘missing link’ between apes and humans that proved Darwinian theories of evolution.
Throughout the 19th and 20th centuries Neanderthals on the page, in museums, and on the screen were portrayed as brutes and rapists. The fantasy novel
Quest for Fire
, written in 1911 by the pseudonymous ‘Joseph-Henri Rosny’, conjured a world of ‘100,000 years ago’ peopled by ‘tribes’ at different evolutionary stages. When a cannibal tribe of ‘coarse brutes’ with ‘raw, heavy flesh, hairy bodies and low foreheads’ steal his clan’s fire, the
Homo sapiens
hero must fight to retrieve it (with the aid of woolly mammoths). In 1981 the novel became an Oscar-winning film, its screenplay written by Anthony Burgess. In the 1990s hair-dragging rape scenes in the
Clan of the Cave Bear
novels (20 million copies sold by 1990) caused the books to be banned from American public libraries.
Neanderthal
was applied to any character, ideology, or practice that was accused of being violent, dull-witted, and backward-looking. Progressive movements in North America applied Neanderthal rhetoric to reactionaries, anti-feminists, and conservatives. Using the international News on the Web corpus, Sahlins reveals a worldwide spike in English-language usage of
Neanderthal
coinciding with Donald Trump’s presidential campaigns.
After the Second World War scientists reacted against the popular caricature of the Neanderthal. In 1953 a Neanderthal who had lived for years with debilitating injuries and who must have been cared for by others was unearthed at Shanidar Cave in Iraq. A few years later another Neanderthal skeleton was found surrounded by flowers as part of an elaborate burial ceremony. These Neanderthals were clearly very different from popular culture’s apish louts.
The mapping of the Neanderthal genome in 2010 showed that Neanderthals are not just among us, but within us. Between 52,000 and 39,000 years ago, humans and Neanderthals interbred repeatedly over a period lasting around 7,000 years, leaving nearly a third of the Neanderthal genome as fragments scattered
49947565.article_summary: 文章评介彼得·萨林斯《我们身边的尼安德特人》，梳理尼安德特人自1856年发现以来在科学与大众文化中的形象演变：从被视为野蛮、低等的“缺环”，到展现照护、埋葬等社会行为的群体。古DNA研究更证明其曾与现代人杂交，部分基因至今存在于人类体内。
49947565.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕尼安德特人与现代人类的基因交流、灭绝原因、文化形象及相关延伸话题展开。

不同观点：
• 基因交流可能存在性别不对称：主要是尼安德特男性与现代人类女性交配，有研究认为或与择偶偏好有关，评论者戏称“尼安德特人很帅”。  
• 有人希望消费基因检测公司在取得同意后公布“尼安德特人基因比例最高”的现代人，以满足好奇心，也可能带来网红收益。  
• 关于灭绝，一种观点认为尼安德特人并非突然被消灭，而是在疾病、竞争和长期通婚中逐渐“被繁育吸收”；该评论进一步类比原住民及其他小族群在全球化下可能面临的基因稀释。  
• 另一研究假说提出，约30万年前现代人扩张可能促成尼安德特人的起源，且尼安德特单倍型后来大多被智人替代；这会使二者更像“兄弟”而非“表亲”，与传统叙述形成争议。  
• 对《Clan of the Cave Bear》的描写存在记忆分歧：有人质疑其因强暴场景被禁，另有人认为书中尼安德特人总体较文明，并不只是野蛮人。

data.title: Page Table Memory Consumption
data.author: shellpipe
data.article_summary: 文章讨论页表的性能与内存开销：树形页表虽利于缓存和TLB填充，但多进程映射同一共享内存时，每个地址空间都需独立PTE，页表开销可与数据甚至超过数据。文中列举网络驱动、数据库、共享内存及MADV_DONTNEED导致页表残留等案例，说明页表内存并非次要问题，并介绍迁移页表、共享页表及回收空页表等解决思路。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：随着系统规模和工作负载变化，页表设计需要重新评估；讨论集中在树形页表与 PowerPC 式哈希页表的取舍，以及页表内存开销。

不同观点：
• **应随问题规模演进**：hinkley认为，2003年正确的方案到2026年可能不再适用，这不代表原设计者犯错。系统规模扩大后，最佳方案可能多次变化，替换旧子系统不等于追责或承认失败。  
• **质疑哈希页表更优的说法**：monocasa指出，文章批评树形页表，却没有充分说明 PowerPC 式哈希页表的优势。哈希表同样要为不同进程保存相同物理页的映射，也会面临 NUMA 布局、部分驻留导致的空间浪费，以及哈希冲突时扩容等问题。  
• **性能取舍存在争议**：哈希页表按虚拟地址分散访问，可能一次带来多个彼此无关的缓存行，增加内存带宽消耗；树形结构抓取相邻 PTE 更有利于缓存和预取。不过哈希表也可能降低某些访问延迟，实际优劣取决于场景。  
• **页表内存可能成为主要负担**：Sopel举例称，Windows 中僵尸进程即使几乎不占普通内存，仍可保留至少32KiB页表；某 AMD 集显驱动漏洞极端情况下甚至可能让页表占据近乎全部内存。  
• **替代方向与调侃**：mastax据此提出多线程可能优于多进程，以减少重复页表；brcmthrowaway则讽刺“AI已经解决所有软件问题”的说法。

补充讨论：核心争议不是“哪种页表绝对正确”，而是不同架构在内存占用、NUMA、缓存局部性、带宽和扩展性之间的权衡。

49916753.article_content:
The other day I was reading
Linus Torvalds punch some people
over hashed page tables. His argument: in a tree, the entries of neighboring pages are adjacent, which means one cache-line fills several TLB entries at once. A hash table, on the other hand, scatters neighbors in buckets:
The fact is, you just don’t know what GOOD actually is.
I’ll tell you: t a
good
TLB fill should pre-populate the TLB with all
the entries it can fit in one cache-line.  Do you realize that a
bog-standard Intel CPU will fetch 8 TLB entries in one go? Together with
a self-mapping (or, as Andy points out, you can just cache the other
levels in dedicated caches), that means that with a single memory
reference you get
eight_times
the coverage that the silly Power hash
tables get.
This discussion happened in 2003, in 1997, on his master’s
thesis
, he explains the adoption of the three multi-level page tables on the kernel. He seemed quite interested in latency, but maybe less interested in memory size:
There are also secondary concerns: the virtual machine memory mappings must be memoryefficient, so that the mapping information does not take up a lot of physical memory that could be used to better advantage for file system caching or running user programs.
In 2020, Shakeel Butt found the exact case where memory efficiency is not a secondary concern at all.
Shakeel
sent a patch adding a page table metric to
memory.stat
.
Roman Gushchin
asked what was the use case for that statistic, arguing page tables are about 1/512 of mapped memory, which is under 1% of most cgroups (“for all but very large cgroups the value will be in the noise of per-cpu counters”). But Shakeel mentioned an
interesting case
he was seeing: a user space network driver that maps application memory for zero copy with a big
pgtables
usage.
Those 1/512 make sense when each page is mapped only once. But if N processes
1
1
To be fair, N should be “address spaces”, not “processes”. Every task
task_struct
has a pointer to an
mm_struct
.
map the same page, each process needs its own PTEs for it. So the page tables cost about N/512 of memory they map. In general terms, this means that if you are running 512 processes with identical PTEs, the page tables cost as much as data pages.
2
2
A data page has 4 KiB. Each PTE has 8 bytes. If 512 processes map the same page, they need 512 PTEs: 512 * 8 = 4 KiB.
Other issues similar to Shakeel’s that I found while searching:
Andrea Arcangeli, 2002.
Andrea found
out why users with 64 GiB x86 machines were running out of memory even though there was a bunch of free memory in the system. Their workloads had hundreds of processes each mapping the same 1 GiB of shared memory. Data pages were shared, and each process needed its own page tables to map them - about 2 MiB with PAE
3
3
x86-32 feature that widens physical addresses to 36 bits allowing 64 GiB of RAM.
. page tables live in the “lowmem” area, in 32-bit x86 that corresponds to ~896 MiB of physical memory. The patch moved the page tables from lowmem to highmem. This was an edge case scenario that only happened because users were using a 32-bit machine - with all the constraints of it, including lowmem - with a feature that allowed them to widen physical addresses. Pretty nice.
Khalid Aziz, 2022.
20 years later,
Khalid reported
a similar problem: an Oracle database server with 512 GB of RAM crashing with OOM when 1500+ clients attached to a 300 GB SGA (shared memory). As in Andrea’s case, data pages were shared, but each process needed its own page tables to map them. With 8-byte PTEs, 2 thousand processes mapping the same 4 KiB page need 16 KB of PTEs for that page. In the worst case, where every process maps the whole SGA, PTEs alone would take 878 GB. He proposed
mshare
to let processes share page tables.
As far as I checked
, no version of mshare has been merged yet.
Qi Zheng, 2021.
Qi reported
a process with 590 GiB RSS and 110 GiB of page tables (!), when mapping that much memory should only need around 1.2 GiB of PTEs. That workload used jemalloc and tcmalloc, which return memory to the kernel with
madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)
instead of
munmap()
4
4
munmap()
at some point calls
free_pgtables
, which ends up calling
free_pgd_range
.
.
MADV_DONTNEED
frees data pages and clears the PTEs, but keeps the page tables allocated, so empty page tables piled up
5
5
Sopel
pointed out on HN
that on Windows “zombie processes may use no memory but still keep >=32KiB page table”. He encountered this himself with
an AMD iGPU driver bug
: “None of the processes that have ever been created finish.” After 100,000 exited
cmd.exe
processes, RAMMap showed about 3.5 GiB of page tables.
. Unlike Andrea’s and Khalid’s cases, there were no shared mappings: it was a single process which kept page tables for freed memory. This patch got several rewrites, and was
merged in 2025
.
While these might read like edge cases from kernel mailing lists, the pattern is common: many processes mapping a large shared memory seg

data.article_summary: 本文介绍一节 Python 图形编程课程：通过画布制作机器人、用循环重复绘制图案，并添加鼠标点击事件实现绘画。课程重点学习函数调用、值、变量、循环和点击事件等基础概念。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对该编程学习/开发产品的评价，集中在定价、产品体验、内容质量及替代方案上。

不同观点：
• **认可其理念与可用性**：ezra60认为 CMU Academy 已很好地实现了类似想法，并且免费提供，是值得参考的替代方案。  
• **批评定价与商业模式**：gnarlouse认为为“AI生成内容”收费49美元近乎敲诈或自我误判；但同时肯定AI显著降低了开发成本，认为应鼓励用AI实现创意，而不应借AI互相牟利。  
• **总体认可产品体验**：aarontian0喜欢其界面和整体表现，并期待未来推出C++版本，表明其对产品方向持积极态度。  
• **质疑内容审核和完成度**：fwip指出产品在征求反馈前应先自行检查，因为第一个任务要求用户完成的内容实际上已经完成，反映出任务设计或测试流程存在明显问题。

补充讨论：评论的争议焦点主要是“AI产品是否值得收费”以及“产品是否经过充分打磨”。一方认可AI带来的低成本和产品体验，另一方则担忧AI内容质量不足、定价过高及借机牟利。
